title: Balanced Thinking
description:
▶ JOIN OUR KICKSTARTER – An Advent Calendar from Cracking the Cryptic – 24 sudoku puzzles by the great and good of the sudoku community! Makes a great holiday gift for yourself or your sudoku-loving friend. https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ctcadventcalendar/an-advent-calendar-from-cracking-the-cryptic

Here's where you can try Balanced X-Sums by Ambrose: https://sudokupad.app/g0gb6ifc1r 
Place an integer from {−3,−2,−1,0,1,2,3} in each cell so that each integer appears exactly once in each row and column.
For a clue outside the grid, let X be the number in the cell closest to it. If X=0, the clue must be 0. If X is greater than 0, the clue equals the sum of the values in the first X cells in that row/column starting at the cell next to the clue. If X is less than 0, the clue equals the sum of the first |X| cells in that row/column starting from the opposite end from the clue.
The answer-check will work using the absolute value of the digits (eg 1 represents 1 or −1).

title: Steer my Crazy Little Robot
description:
Pledge to our KickStarter and get yourself an Advent Calendar from CtC: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ctcadventcalendar/an-advent-calendar-from-cracking-the-cryptic

Here's where you can attempt The Little Robot's Crayon by Kainapple: https://sudokupad.app/05toqchwta 
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
A robot is moving around the grid in an endless loop, and does the following: 1. Checks the digit it's standing on,  2. Moves that many cells forward,  3. Turns 90° clockwise (on the spot), 4. Repeat. You can see the robot moving east, but it's not clear which cell it checked to start that move. The robot never checks a digit that would instruct it to cross an X or leave the grid.
An X joins digits that sum to 10. A white dot joins consecutive digits. A black dot joins digits where one is double the other. The robot shades in any white dots it walks directly over, changing them into black dots (that never had to have a consecutive relationship at all!). The robot may re-enter a cell during the loop only if it never turns in that cell.

title: The "Single Line" Miracle Sudoku
description:
*** ADVENT CALENDAR KICKSTARTER HERE ***
Get the ultimate Christmas present for a puzzler here:

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ctcadventcalendar/an-advent-calendar-from-cracking-the-cryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A truly remarkable conception tonight from Matt Tressel called Rooms And Regions. Incredibly a single "region sum line" allows the puzzle to be solved with no given digits. This one was recommended by Dorlir and with very good reason!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/wtfa2dqnkz

Rules
Divide the grid into four non-overlapping regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Each region contains the digits 1–9 once each. Digits don't repeat in any row or column. All outside cells that contain a line must also contain a digit. That digit will appear in the Nth position of the corresponding row or column when looking into the grid from the direction of the clue-cell where N is the first digit seen from that direction. Region and grid borders divide the blue line into segments. Each segment of the line must have the same sum.

title: Solve A Variant Sudoku In Under 3 Minutes?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Mark challenged Simon to solve this lovely little puzzle by James Sinclair called 10k in under 3 minutes so we could use it on our social media platforms to advertise the wonders of variant sudoku!! James made this to celebrate his milestone achievement of obtaining 10,000 subscribers for his sudoku newsletter (linked below) - well done James!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/10k

Rules
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply (place the digits 1-6, once each, in every row, column and bold-outlined box).
The product of the digits inside the cage is equal to 10000. Digits can repeat within the cage if allowed by other rules.
At least one of the four corner cells must contain 3.

description:

title: The Ballroom: Another Sudoku Gem!
description:
*** ADVENT CALENDAR KICKSTARTER HERE ***
Get the ultimate Christmas present for a puzzler here:

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ctcadventcalendar/an-advent-calendar-from-cracking-the-cryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
ChinStrap returns to the channel tonight with a much-recommended sudoku called Ballroom. This is just sublime. Multi-layered, interesting and lovely. 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/mvn7atnxaz

Rules
Divide the grid into four non-overlapping regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Each region contains the digits 1–9 once each. Digits don't repeat in any row or column. A digit in a circle (both inside and outside the grid) counts how many circles contain that digit. A circled outside cell gives the digit in the Nth cell looking into the grid, where N is the digit in the first cell. The first N cells for a clued row/column are all in the same region (and the (N+1)th cell, if there is one, is in a different region).

title: The Mad Thermometer [Sudoku Of The Year?]
description:
*** ADVENT CALENDAR KICKSTARTER HERE ***
Get the ultimate Christmas present for a puzzler here:

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ctcadventcalendar/an-advent-calendar-from-cracking-the-cryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Sometimes Mark asks Simon to open a puzzle live on camera to get his reaction to seeing the sudoku for the first time. Tonight is one such occasion! The puzzle in question is called Long Multiplication by basilicon - a new name to us. As you'll see if you watch the video, this is one of Simon's favourite puzzles of the year.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/1emqz1uqso

Rules
Divide the grid into nine non-overlapping regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally-connected cells. Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 such that no number repeats in any row, column, or region. Each row/column/region contains one "multiplier" cell. The nine multiplier cells all contain different digits. A cell's VALUE is its digit multiplied by the digit in its region's multiplier cell. VALUES along a thermometer increase from the bulb.

title: Is this one of the Greatest Loops?
description:
Here's where you can attempt The Greatest Loop by ThePedallingPianist: https://sudokupad.app/1xuvxocdoi 
Place 1-6 in each row, column and 3x2 box. Draw a loop that moves orthogonally between the centres of some cells and does not visit any cell more than once. For any cell in which the loop turns, the digit on that loop corner is strictly greater than the sum of the adjacent digits on the loop.
Cells with a circle are not visited by the loop, and contain a digit showing how many of the (up to 8) surrounding cells are visited by the loop.

*** ADVENT CALENDAR KICKSTARTER HERE ***

Jonesy returns to the channel tonight with a magnificent sudoku featuring a really rather brilliant chaos construction idea and killer cages. It's not too difficult but it just feels great to solve! Enjoy.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/w4wnsq4p8k

Rules
Place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and region. Each region consists of nine orthogonally connected cells. Regions cannot overlap. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the value given in the top left corner of the cage. A digit inside a cage indicates how many cells of its own region it "sees" in its row and column, including itself. Region borders block vision. If two adjacent digits inside the same cage have the same parity (ie both are odd or both are even), they belong to the same region. If they have different parity, they belong to separate regions. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one digit is double the other.

Here's where you can try Counting Shadows by Andrea Acciatelli (Cliffhanger resolved in tonight's episode!): https://sudokupad.app/1vyiko0v3g 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In each 3×3 box, shade every cell whose digit matches its position within that box, counting from left to right, top to bottom. For example, R6C4 is the 7th cell in Box 5, so it must be shaded if it contains a 7.
Each line has a circle. The digit in the circle indicates the total number of shaded cells along its connected line, including the circle's own cell if shaded.
Each medium-sized white circle contains one or two digits that must appear, at least once, within the four cells surrounding it.
Kropki Dots: A white dot connects two digits that are consecutive. A black dot connects two digits where one is double the other. All Kropki dots connecting cells belonging to DIFFERENT LINES are given. However, Kropki connections between cells belonging to the SAME LINE may exist, without being shown.

title: Why Does My 3-cell Sudoku Cage Sum to 27?!
description:
*** ADVENT CALENDAR KICKSTARTER HERE ***
Get the ultimate Christmas present for a puzzler here:

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ctcadventcalendar/an-advent-calendar-from-cracking-the-cryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
After yesterday's sensational fog sudoku by Michael Lefkowitz, we attempt another tonight by Isamook. This one features the rarely encountered Psycho Killer Cages - which are quite funny given their totals. Enjoy!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/vxtt08627z

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a digit may or may not clear fog. Psycho Killer Cages: The clue in the top-left corner of a red cage is the sum of the digits in the "target cells" pointed at by the digits inside the cage itself. Each digit inside a cage acts as a pointer to its target cell as follows: a) The digit N placed in a cage cell dictates that the target cell resides in the Nth 3x3 box (boxes are numbered in normal reading order); b) Within that Nth 3x3 box, the target cell occupies the exact same relative position as the pointer cell occupies within its own 3×3 box. Eg if r1c3 was an 8, its value so far as the cage sum is concerned would be the digit in r7c6 (which is in Box 8 and is in the same relative position (position 3) as the pointer cell, r1c3). Zipper lines: Digits an equal distance from the centre of a lavender line must sum to the digit in the central cell of the line (which is marked with a lavender dot).

title: Phistomefel: The Sudoku Genius
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Phistomefel is a genius. We have concluded this over the years of doing battle with his puzzles but, if possible, over time he just seems to get cleverer. Tonight's extraordinary offering is one of his most mad and brilliant sudokus...

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/mvk3xv23yc

Rules
Divide the grid into 8 regions, each consisting of 8 orthogonally-connected cells. Regions may wrap around the grid's edges, both horizontally and vertically. Each row, column, and region contains the digits 1 to 8 exactly once. Some region boundaries are given and have to be respected. The digits along an arrow sum to the digit in its circle. The digits 1 to 3 are small and the digits 6 to 8 are large. Any two orthogonally adjacent cells separated by a region border must contain one small and one large digit. This includes cells in different regions at opposite edges of the grid, since the grid wraps.

title: The Sudoku Tells The Greatest Lies
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What a combination of brains there are behind tonight's sudoku! Marty Sears and Dorlir unite to produce The Greatest Lies... a puzzle whose main line looks extremely dubious indeed. This is wonderful as is Darren's story during the introduction.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/lobbo5pxv4

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every row, column and 3x3 box contains one liar cell, whose real value is different from its digit. Every liar cell contains a different digit from 1-9. Every liar cell has a different value from 1-9. One cell on each olive line contains the greatest value on that line, which is greater than the sum of any other pair of values on that line. If a black dot sits between two cells, the value of one is double the value of the other. If an X sits between two cells, their values sum to 10. NOTES: In each green arrow, enter the liar digit for its row, and in the circle to its right, write its real value.

title: Phistomefel's Controversial Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've received a lot of emails about this one! Apparently it is much more difficult than first believed and lots of you have requested we have a go at it. Simon can absolutely confirm that, for him at least, while this is assuredly another beautiful puzzle from the sudoku demon, it's also quite hard!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/dmj8j1evq1

Rules
Write the digits from 1 to 6 into the cells of the grid such that no digit repeats in a row, column, or region. The six regions, each consisting of six orthogonally connected cells, have to be determined. Some region boundaries are given and have to be respected. The cells on a purple line contain a set of distinct, (normally, not cyclically) consecutive digits, in any order. For digits 1–6, cyclic consecutive means the next digit in the cycle 1→2→3→4→5→6→1. If two orthogonally adjacent cells are separated by a region boundary, the bottom digit must be cyclic consecutive to the top digit, or the right digit must be cyclic consecutive to the left digit, respectively.

title: The Lines that are Hidden TWICE!
description:
Here's where you can try Hidden German Whisper: Trinity by 72kchunshuai: https://sudokupad.app/h47xuwt40l 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Correctly placing digits may clear some fog. Digits increase from the bulb end of a thermo. Digits on a purple line form a set of consecutive digits, in any order. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum. 
Lines mentioned above may only move from center to center. They may overlap only at endpoints, but never cross. Renban and Region Sum Lines cannot overlap with their own kind (even at endpoints), so each is a single line.
All (and only) the cells connected together by lines mentioned above belong to the same Region. Digits MAY repeat within the same region. Hidden beneath each region is at least one German Whisper line. Each German Whisper line is at least THREE cells long, and lies entirely beneath the lines mentioned above. Adjacent digits along a German Whisper line must differ by at least 5.

▶ OUR PATREON PAGE – JOIN THE COMMUNITY, SUPPORT US AND TRY OUR PUZZLE HUNTS◀

title: It's a real Uphill Struggle
description:
Here's where you can try Uphill Struggle by Trufflebear: https://sudokupad.app/ir256dson1 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade each cell in the grid using one of two colours, such that all cells with the same colour are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 square of cells is entirely one colour. Black dots between cells indicate that their digits are in a 1:2 ratio. The digits along a red arrow sum to the digit in its circle.
The yin-yang colour boundary (when discovered) splits the line into segments, each of which is a separate Thermo line, all running in the same direction. Put another way, digits on this line increase continuously from the bulb, unless the line crosses a colour boundary, in which case the digit after the boundary may be lower than the one before it. All segments are either 3, 4 or 5 cells long.

title: A Brilliant Sudoku/Puzzle Mash-up
description:
Here's where you can have a go at Dutch Masyu by Yttrio: https://sudokupad.app/jov93r0b6g  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single non-intersecting loop that moves orthogonally through the centers of some cells, that passes through every circle clue. The loop must turn on black circles and pass straight through the cells on either side. The loop must go straight through white circles and turn in at least one of the cells on either side. The loop acts as a Dutch Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 4). The digit in each given circle clue counts the total number of loop cells in all straight loop segments coming off of the cell (counting the cells where the loop turns, and counting the clued cell itself once).

▶ OUR PATREON PAGE – JOIN THE COMMUNITY, SUPPORT US AND TRY OUR PUZZLE HUNTS◀

title: The Sudoku Expert's Favourite Rule
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Dr Logic has made a sensational sudoku called Line Dancing which one of our testers in particular loved so much she insisted we try it on the channel! It features the "exclusive" rule but in a slightly new way and relying on rather beautiful graphics... 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/7d1rkyffv3

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a red line, digits alternate parity (ie odds/evens must alternate.) Along a lavender line, any pair of digits that are the same distance from the centre of the line (marked by a spot) sum to the same total. For odd length lines, the total is the central digit. Digits on a pink line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits, in any order. Adjacent digits along a green line differ by at least 5. Each line belongs to a group. These groups are denoted by smaller coloured lines within the larger lines. The groups are: 'white, black, blue, red'. Within a group, digits placed on these lines cannot repeat (e.g, there cannot be two 4s in red, etc.) If two digits are separated by a black dot then one digit is double the other; if two digits are separated by a white dot those digits are consecutive.

title: One Tough Cookie: A "Cat Run" Puzzle!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The Feeding Friendsy series of puzzles in which some of the world's best setters imitate the style of Marty Sears' Rat Run sudokus has been incredibly so far. Tonight Simon attempts Number 8 (of 10) which is called One Tough Cookie by blackjackfitz. It's named appropriately but is seriously interesting and cunning. Just try to keep all the rules in your head :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/pn630t41aj

Rules
Fill the grid with the digits 1-9... there's more to it but we'll get there.
#FRIENDSHIPGOALS
If you give blackcatfitz a cookie... he's going to ask for some milk! Help him reach the milk by finding a path through the maze of sweet treats. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any thick caramel walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, blackcatfitz may move diagonally — if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so — but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall.
SOMEDOKU
Fill every row 'n' and column 'n' with exactly 'n' different digits, chosen from the digits 1-9, repeating as necessary.
CHAOS CONSTRUCTION
Divide the grid into nine (9) regions, each containing nine (9) orthogonally connected cells. Given caramel walls always separate two different regions; however, any isolated, rounded wall pillars may exist wholly within one region.
COOKIES
The digit in a cookie indicates how many different digits appear in its region. For example, a digit 6 in a cookie indicates that the region includes 6 distinct digits (and therefore 3 repeats). No two cookies contain the same digit.
DARK CHOCOLATE CHIPS
Cells sharing a dark chocolate chip must belong to the SAME region. Digits separated by a dark chocolate chip have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other). 
WHITE CHOCOLATE CHIPS
Cells sharing a white chocolate chip must belong to DIFFERENT regions. Digits separated by a white chocolate chip are consecutive. 
CRANBERRIES
Note that blackcatfitz is allergic to cranberries — you must not include them on his path! If a cranberry sits between two digits one will be even and one will be odd. 
TRIALS AND TRAILS
In this test of friendship, blackcatfitz must retrieve each of the nine cookies in numerical order (from 1-9) before returning to enjoy the milk. Good luck!

*** BRAND NEW COMPETITION ON PATREON ***
On 1 October we released a brand new Sudoku Hunt competition on Patreon. There's 8 puzzles to solve by 20 October to win the chance to come onto the channel and solve a puzzle with us! title: Darkness and eventually ... Light
description:
Here's where you can try Darkness and Light by HalfBakedLunatic: https://sudokupad.app/zvf2imrgu5 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot must have consecutive digits; on a black dot, one digit is double the other. ALL POSSIBLE DOTS ARE GIVEN (a 1:2 combination may have either colour of dot).
Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 cluster of cells is entirely shaded or unshaded. Orthogonally adjacent cells which separate shaded and unshaded regions must contain digits that differ by at least 3. Heavy black lines denote separation between shaded and unshaded regions. Cells separated by an X must have digits that sum to 10. For each X, both cells are either in the shaded or unshaded region. Not all X's are shown.

title: Some Special Lines - in London?
description:
Here's where you can try Sissa visits London by Patrick Junke: https://sudokupad.app/aojv6vyqzk  
Normal sudoku rules apply. A correct digit placed in a cell clears the fog around it.
Sissa's Lines: Each line has a beginning and an end, but neither is marked. Every cell on a line has an associated value. Starting from the beginning of the line, each cell’s value is twice the value of the previous cell. The digit in each cell is the digital root of its value: keep adding the digits of the number until you get a single digit from 1 to 9.
Example: A cell with value 32 contains 5 (3 + 2 = 5). The next cell has value 64 and therefore contains 1 (6 + 4 = 10 → 1 + 0 = 1).
On each line, exactly one cell matches its value.

title: To Finish This Sudoku You Must NOT Finish It??!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A very unusual debut on the channel tonight for Berdy whose puzzle Schrödoku requires you to not be able to finish it in order to finish it correctly!! This requires some careful thinking and it's quite easy (at least Simon believes) to make a logical error!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/zweh6b2lya

Rules
Fill uncaged cells with the digits 1-9 such that the digits 1-9 do not repeat in any row, column or 3x3 box. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. Digits along a purple line form a set of consecutive digits without repeats in any order. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in cells joined by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Schrödinger's cages: cells in cages must never be "observed" (collapsed to a single value by normal sudoku rules). For example, a caged cell that sees every digit 1-8 could only be a 9 and is considered "observed". Fill in every cell outside the cages so that no caged cell collapses to a single value. Exactly one fill keeps the caged cells unobserved.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
These are the halcyon days of sudoku. In the last few weeks we've seen incredible puzzle after incredible puzzle and tonight Phistomefel's new one, Roundabout, is another work of art. Can you understand this type of Phistomefel Ring?!

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Without wanting to say too much about it, this sudoku (Loopy Tiles by Marty Sears) is one of the most memorable Simon can remember solving. It is absolutely fascinating and we're looking forward to the comments on how you all solve it!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/zusdr2z05v

Rules
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Use the 7 types of tile shown at the top to tile the whole grid, so that a picture of a single blue loop is formed. The blue loop moves orthogonally between cells. A digit in a circle indicates how many times that cell's tile type appears in the grid. (Tiles may not be rotated.) If a yellow dot sits between two digits, they are non-consecutive digits. title: When Your Sudoku Rat Run Involves A Famished Flamingo!?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Firstly let's congratulate the constructor of tonight's puzzle, Stuart (aka ThePedallingPianist) and his wife Alannah, on the arrival of their twin sons last Thursday! Simon decides that today would therefore be a very suitable day to attempt a new puzzle in the Feeding FriendsY series, this one called The Sincerest Form Of Flattery. It's fair to say that this sudoku is absolutely mad. No-one could claim any different... but is it solvable? That is the question!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/nh9ef1t01i

Rules
SQUISHDOKU:
The grid is divided into nine 3x3 boxes, which overlap on dashed lines. Place a digit from 1-9 in each cell such that there are no repeats in any rows, columns or boxes.
#FRIENDSHIPGOALS:
Fletcher the Flat-Bellied Flamingo is feeling famished! He only eats food if it has been squished; so help to draw a path for him through the nice, flat pancakes to fatten him up, as he makes his way to bed for a post-pancake nap.
The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any thick, brown crust walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Fletcher may move diagonally — if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so — but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall.
TELEPORTS: 
Entering a red teleport will cause Fletcher to be instantly transported to the other teleport. From there he can continue his journey. The teleports contain the same digit.
TRIALS AND TRAILS:
In this test of friendship, every segment of Fletcher's path contained entirely within a 3x3 box is an Index Line. These segments may overlap, meaning some cells may be part of multiple Index Lines (For example, r3c1 would be part of a segment in box 1 and part of a segment in box 4). The digit in the Nth cell of an Index Line indicates the position of the digit N on that segment. Positions are counted starting from the first cell visited on the segment. Good luck!

title: Incredible 100% "Perfect" Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What a beautiful sudoku we have this evening from yttrio called Double Equality Yin Yang. Even though it's been around for a few weeks, it still boasts a 100% rating (and 4/5 stars for difficulty) - which is incredibly hard to do. Wonderful from start to finish.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/peoe36s43j

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply.
Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded.
Digits in shaded cells count as double their value for the purposes of sums. Digits in unshaded cells count their normal value.
Digits cannot repeat in cages (though effective values may repeat, such as a doubled 1 and regular 2). Every cage contains at least one shaded cell and one unshaded cell. In each cage, the sum of values in shaded cells equals the sum of values in unshaded cells.

title: The Sudoku With Chocolate And Banana?!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
ChinStrap's new sudoku, Dutch Chocolate Banabner, has been recommended to us by many of you and we understand why. This is a brilliantly constructed puzzle that is just a joy to solve. 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/a48228snwx?setting-nogrid=1

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Choco-banana: Shade some cells such that every group of orthogonally connected shaded cells is a rectangle (chocolate), and every group of orthogonally connected unshaded cells is not a rectangle (banana). Note: squares are rectangles. In every chocolate region, orthogonally adjacent cells must differ by at least 4. In every banana region, no two digits are equal or consecutive. A digit in a circle counts the number of cells of the chocolate or banana region that circle lies in.

title: The AI-Resistant Homework!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy birthday to MathGuy_12, one of the authors of tonight's puzzle - along with ChinStrap! The sudoku itself is called Split At Birth - one of the more colourful offerings we've seen - it's got some highly original logic too! Simon wonders whether, in this age where AI can answer (almost) everything - schools should be thinking more about giving pupils puzzles for homework... what could be more fun? (And more AI-proof?)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/fvdkiaq6vi?setting-nogrid=true

Rules
Place five copies of each digit 1-9 in the grid. All five copies of the same digit must be in cells that are orthogonally connected. To fit all the digits into the grid, some cells are 'S-cells' that contain two DISTINCT digits. If a cell has one digit, write it in the top left corner. In an S-cell, write the smaller digit top-left and the larger bottom-right. Split Gene Lines: The sum of all digits in cells on a DNA strand is equal to the concatenation of the 2-4 digits in the zygote cells at the end of the strands in some order. For example if the zygotes were a 38 and a 49 s-cell, then 9348 would be a valid sum for the line.

description:
Here's where you can try Wedding Day by Jack Isaac Bryan: https://sudokupad.app/q6e8matn0v
Jack and Arathi are getting married! Complete the puzzle to escort Arathi down the aisle.
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the total shown. Neighbouring digits on a green line differ by 5 or more. Neighbouring digits on an orange line differ by 4 or more. Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into an archipelago of 9 islands, separated by a continuous, orthogonally-connected area of water. Islands cannot touch, even at a corner, and no 2x2 area can be entirely water. The circles are all situated on an island and a circle's digit denotes the number of cells that island occupies. The circled digits constitute a full set of the digits 1 to 9. Digits cannot repeat on an island.
On a black dot, one digit is double the other and all black dots link cells that are either both island cells or both water cells.

title: Never Mind The Swordfish... Here's The Sudoku Dolphin!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In a week of extraordinary puzzles, we return to the fantastic Feeding FriendsY series in which some of the world's great constructors imitate Marty Sears' Rat Run sudokus. This one is called Fintastic Voyage by ChinStrap and it's a super-clever imitation of Marty himself. Original, intricate and witty!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/udeje6c23i

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
#FRIENDSHIPGOALS:
Help FinStrap the Dolphin reach the fish by finding a path through the ocean! The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any thick coral wall.
As well as moving orthogonally, FinStrap may move diagonally — if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so — but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall.
SEAWEED: 
Digits separated by green seaweed have a difference of at least 5. Not all seaweed is given.
BLACK SEA URCHINS: 
Digits separated by black sea urchins have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other). Not all sea urchins are given.
TRIALS and TRAILS:
FinStrap needs oxygen and his path will track how much he has left.  Digits along the path must strictly decrease.  When FinStrap either enters a bubble cell or jumps into the air (all cells in row 1), the path may reset to any value (and start decreasing again after that).  If FinStrap does jump into the air, he must immediately enter water again. 
FUN SCIENCE FACT:
Fish are not oxygen - the path constraint must still be obeyed when reaching the fish.

description:
Here's where you can try Not Constraints by Derek LeClair: https://sudokupad.app/u5f00lj0dt 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A pair of adjacent digits along a red line must not have opposite parity (even/odd). A pair of adjacent digits along a thermometer must not increase as they move away from the bulb end. A peach line must not contain one low (123), one middle (456), and one high (789) digit. On a gray line, digits must not be between the digits in the circles on the ends. Digits on a blue diagonal line must repeat along the blue diagonal line. On a black dot, neither digit is double the other. On a white dot, digits are not consecutive. Digits separated by an X do not sum to 10.

title: Counting Circles - How Many Times?
description:
Here's where you can try Ramor by Aeon: https://sudokupad.app/ec2ufpzyp1 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Values along an arrow sum to the digit in a circled cell attached to it. A digit on a circle (also including arrow circles) indicates the number of circles containing that digit. In cages, values sum to the indicated total in top-left corner.
Each row, column and box contains exactly one tripler cell (digits in tripler cells CAN repeat): if a tripler is in non-circled cell, the value of the cell is 3x that digit; if a tripler is in a circled cell the value of the digit is unchanged - instead, it triples the amount of instances for the counting circles purposes. Example: If a 5 is in a circle and a tripler cell, it counts for 3 of the 5 instances 5 needs to appear in circles.

title: All Aboard the Sudoku Express
description:
Get these aliens home! Try Sudoku Express by Mbumbee and Synergenesis here: https://sudokupad.app/ui5rcvo0p1 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a line to pick up three aliens and drop them off in their homes. The two purple aliens (R4C5 and R6C5) must each be dropped off in one of the two purple homes (R1C1 and R1C9), while the orange alien (R5C5) must be dropped off in the orange home (R9C5). The line starts in R9C1 and ends in R5C9, moving orthogonally. It does not visit any cell more than once, nor cross its own path or go through an alien or an alien home. You must pick up an alien when the path orthogonally touches that alien's cell unless there are already two aliens being carried. You automatically drop off an alien when the path orthogonally touches a matching home cell, if no alien is already in that home. On the line, the total sum is the same for each box visited (even by different segments), and this sum is the product of the digits on the aliens. 
Cells separated by an X and V sum to 10 and 5 respectively and are not on the path EVERY possible X and V where both cells are not along the path is given. Every alien home has a cell with an even digit. Each digit shown on a quadruple clue appears at least once in its four surrounding cells. A digit listed twice must appear at least twice in the surrounding four cells.

title: Simple Rule = Fantastic Sudoku Variant
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears returns to the channel tonight with This Hits Different, an absolutely lovely twist on hitlines in which the all line totals need to be unique. There's such a variety of logic in this one, it really is a delight to solve.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/xvrdqbvla1

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat on a beige hitline. The 'hit total' of a hitline is the sum of any digits that match their position along the line, starting from the square (which is position 1.) Eg: A line reading 8214 would have a hit total of 6, the sum of 2 and 4 (2 is in the 2nd position and 4 is in the 4th position.) In this puzzle, no two hitlines have the same hit total.

title: The Most Terrifying Lines In Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight's sudoku is so difficult that Marty Sears even warned Simon about it! It's part of the Feeding Friendsy series in which some of the world's best puzzle makers imitate Marty's Rat Run style. This one is called A Byte To Eat and it's by Scojo, who decided for some (mad) reason to implement a puzzle using "robot lines". These are the most awkward things to get your head around... as Simon finds out!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/hba1a9t660

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Help Scobot reach the battery by finding a path through the maze! Your path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Scobot may move diagonally — if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so — but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall. Scobot may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between. If two digits are separated by a gear one is double the other. In this puzzle, the path acts as a 'robot line', along which Scobot can move forwards and backwards.  Scobot begins by inspecting the digit in his own cell. This tells him how many cells along his path he must move. The digit he stops on also gets inspected, and again tells him how many cells he must move. This time he can move in either direction, backwards or forwards, as long as there is enough room to move the correct distance (he may never overshoot the beginning or end of the path, and he can't reverse direction mid-movement). He keeps repeating this process until he has inspected every cell along his path, without ever stopping at the same cell more than once. He will finish by stopping at the battery (the digit on the battery does not need to be inspected and so is of little importance.) For clarity, Scobot and the battery are the physical ends of the path, as well as being the first and last cells visited. Furthermore, Scobot may never re-enter a box once he has left it, not even by reversing back along the path, so he must be thorough and finish all of his inspections in a box before moving on.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy birthday sujoyku who set tonight's puzzle, Fernwirkung. This is a very cool twist on killer sudoku that is garnering a lot of love from the puzzle community. Remember to check out Patreon today too for our brand new competition!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yvysiky0z8

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must not repeat and no two cages may sum to the same total.  No cage sums to its own clue, but receives help from exactly one other cage. title: How Would A Mathematician Solve This?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely astonishing idea and execution from Kaktuslav tonight called Wekiera (some sort of Polish weapon we believe). Simon does his best with it but suspects mathematicians might be able to "see" a different approach. The comments might be interesting!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9mnu386ybb

Rules
Choose six distinct digits from 1 to 9 and divide the grid into six orthogonally connected regions of six cells each. Place the chosen digits so that each row, column, and region contains each digit exactly once. The three digits in the pill form a three-digit number, read from left to right, equal to the sum of all digits on the arrow shaft. Region borders divide the shaft into segments of equal sum. title: Straight into the Vortex ... and Back out Again!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Reflective Vortex by Julink: https://sudokupad.app/5ea8g3bxow 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide a blue line into segments which have the same sum. Different lines may have different sums.
Mirrors are placed on cells as thin grey lines. A mirror reflects everything in its viewed row and column. This means that every digit reflected by a mirror cannot appear on the reflected part of the row or column. Mirrors only have one reflective side, it is up to the player to determine which side of each mirror is the reflective one.
Example: If the mirror in R4C7 had its reflective side facing South-East, then the digits in R4C8 and R4C9 could not appear in R5C7, R6C7, R7C7, R8C7 and R9C7.

title: What If A Sudoku Contained Zeroes? Lots Of Zeroes??!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A very very clever debut puzzle on the channel tonight from Invi and his sudoku Zero Sum. The twist on normal sudoku rules is simple but deadly and leads to some original and fascinating logic. Not at all easy but extremely rewarding!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9iskh68h4z

Rules
Fill the grid with the digits 0-9 such that each of the digits 1-9 appear at most once in any row, column or box. The digit 0 may appear any number of times in the grid. For every row, column, and box, its digits must sum to the total number of zeroes in the puzzle. The 3x3 region borders divide the blue line into segments with each segment having the same sum . Cells separated by an X sum to ten. Arrows between cells point to the smaller digit.

title: Help SAVE The Independent Cryptic Crossword
description:
Simon was shocked to learn, on Saturday, that The Independent newspaper is considering no longer publishing a daily cryptic crossword. The Independent's crossword is one of the very best in the country - they have an excellent stable of setters and a great editor. 

With the boom in the popularity of mind sports/puzzles and a whole new generation of younger solvers finding their way to cryptic crosswords due  to the success of minutecryptic (and even this channel), it seems such a shame. 

We're hoping that, if the managing editor of The Independent, Richard Best, finds out how much love there is for the puzzle, perhaps, he could be persuaded to reconsider any decision. His email address is:

managingeditor@independent.co.uk

if you'd like to make your views known.

title: Don't Worry about the Wet Blankets!
description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Two values divided by V sum to 5. Two values divided by X sum to 10. On a black dot, one value is double the other. The value in the grey circle is odd. Values in a Killer Cage sum to the total given on the top left corner of the cage, if given. Digits or values MAY repeat in a cage if allowed by other rules. title: No Complicated Rules So How Can This Solve?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Jigakuro makes a debut on the channel tonight with an absolutely remarkable fog-of-war sudoku called Rainbow Arrows In Fog. It is quite miraculous that you can deduce remotely sufficient information from the starting position to achieve anything, let alone a unique solution. This is just remarkable.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/297mtjab6j

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits clears the fog in the surrounding 3x3 area. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. All arrows of the same colour are a different length. Arrows do not cross or overlap or branch. All colors are significantly different and colourblind friendly. Lines are too thin to be visible in crossed corners. No guessing is required, nor is any squinting!

*** BRAND NEW COMPETITION ON PATREON ***
On 1 September we released a new Sudoku Hunt competition on Patreon. The solution videos are now out! Simon has also completed a series of videos attempting a very challenging cryptic crossword called Periodic Location by Nebuchadnezzar. (This is a five video series!)

title: No Peeking - I Mean it!
description:
Here's where you can try No Peeking - Markov's Order by Belamis: https://sudokupad.app/llgqh0kzve but do make sure you understand the rules first!
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Digits MUST be placed in visible cells only. Placing a digit in the last visible cell will reveal the next set of cells. Digits in this puzzle must be placed in the correct order (And this requires thinking ahead). Each digit you place must be a factor or multiple of the previously placed digit. E.g. since the first placed (given) digit is 4, the next placed digit must be selected from 1,2,4,8. Digits may be placed in any order once ALL fog is revealed.
Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. Digits do not repeat in cages, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner.

title: A Short Circuit in my Brain
description:
Here's where you can try Switching circuit by Neil Armchair: https://sudokupad.app/fplfqjp556 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw two lines: one connecting the cells marked “A” and one connecting the cells marked “B”. The lines can only move orthogonally and do not enter cells with a blue square or a yellow diamond. Each other cell can be visited only once.
For each line, box borders will divide the line into segments which each have the same sum N. Each line segment must have a unique combination of digits. Different permutations of the same digits are not considered unique. 
If you rotate the middle 3x3 box of the puzzle by 180 degrees, you should still have exactly two lines (i.e. no loose ends or isolated loops anywhere in the diagram). However, now both lines connect an “A” to a “B”. After rotation, the two lines are no longer valid unique region sum lines. The digit in a blue square indicates the number of cells directly around it (orthogonally and diagonally) that are visited by a line before rotating the switch. The digit in a yellow triangle indicates the number of cells in the direction of the arrow that are visited by a line.

title: Sudoku Expert Gets Destroyed By Tom Cruise Character?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Deckatron has made a remarkable sudoku riffing on the low-flying aircraft character, Maverick, who seems to spend most of his days buzzing past Simon's attic window. Can you find the loop that Maverick enjoys making? And can you forgive Simon for attempting this puzzle while a bit under the weather?! 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/f9jwzjz6ug

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Simon's House is in Row 5 Column 5. All Houses (including Simon's) act as Counting Circles.  If a digit, N, appears on a House, it appears exactly N times on all Houses. Draw a continuous loop around the grid that represents Maverick's Flight Plan. The loop may move in any direction (orthogonally and diagonally).  
The loop does not enter the same cell more than once or cross itself except over Simon's House. Maverick loves to fly over Simon's House, and does so FOUR times during his Flight Plan.  (e.g. the loop enters and leaves the middle cell 4 times). Region borders break up the Flight Plan in segments, with each segment having the same sum.
Each time the Flight Plan enters any Region, it travels over exactly ONE House.  (Clarification: Region 5 will have four separate segments each with the same sum and each including the digit on Simon's house). 
A Red X separates two digits that sum to 10 and the flight plan does NOT cross it. 
A Green Arrow points to the smaller digit it sits between and the flight plan does cross it, traveling in the direction of the Arrow. 
Maverick's current position is shown by the plane and is on the loop.

title: Can You Identify This Puzzle's Author?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Ok he might have signed it and given us a clue but that's not the point! Marty Sears has made another stunner in the form of Yin Yang Yogn - a wrogn puzzle with some gorgeous ideas in it... and the best compliment we can give it is to say "it's definitely a Marty sudoku!" :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/o9rylnnnw1

Rules
Divide the grid into three regions, each consisting of orthogonally connected cells. No 2x2 area can be entirely within one region. Clues always sit entirely within one region. For two of the regions, all of its clues tell the truth, obeying the rules listed below. But the 3rd region is a liar region. All of the clues in the liar region break their rule. CLUES TYPES: a) If a V sits between two digits, they sum to 5; b) If a BLACK DOT sits between two digits, one is double the other; c) If a WHITE DOT sits between two digits, they are consecutive; d) If a YELLOW SQUARE sits between two digits, they are not consecutive; e)If a GREEN DIAMOND sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5; f) If a RED DOT sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even; and g) A digit in a CIRCLE indicates the sum of all the digits seen in the direction of its arrow that are in the same region as the circle, until the first region border is reached.

title: Explore the Mystery City
description:
Here's where you can try Mystery City Sandwich by Molly Boodey: https://sudokupad.app/392kqguq3f 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits outside the grid are either X-sum values, skyscraper values, or sandwich values. The outermost grid digit of a row or column fully determines if the outside value is a X-sum, skyscraper, or sandwich. For example, if R1C5 is a 5 and column 5’s outer value of 15 is determined to be an X-sum clue, then every outermost grid digit 5 is being acted on by an X-sum clue. 
X-Sums: Clues outside the grid give the sum of the first X numbers placed in the corresponding row or column, where X is digit in the cell next to the X-sum clue.
Skyscraper: Grid digits represent skyscrapers with heights equal to their values. Taller buildings hide shorter ones behind them. Clues outside the grid show how many skyscrapers are visible from that side in the indicated row or column.
Sandwich: Digits between 1 and 9 in the row or column must sum to the clue outside the grid.

title: These Rat Run Sudokus Are Hard!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight Simon attempts the fourth puzzle in the new series of Rat Run sudokus in which Marty Sears' friends tried to imitate his style for his birthday. This one is A Slither Of Cake by Lake and its 5* difficulty rating is definitely deserved. Very interesting, very challenging and VERY easy to make a mistake!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/g7j9xbggr4

Rules
Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that digits don't repeat in a row, column or 3x3 box (marked with dotted lines).
FRIENDSHIPGOALS:
It's time to party like it's 1997! Help Snaake the... snake take the cake - make a path that is not fake! The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, Snaake may move diagonally — if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so — but may never pass diagonally through the squared end / corner of a wall.
WORMHOLES: 
Entering a Wormhole will cause Snaake to be instantly transported to the matching coloured Wormhole. From there he can continue his journey. Wormholes are not required to share digits.
ONE-WAY DOORS: 
Snaake may only pass directly through a dark green arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between.
WHITE PELLETS:
Digits separated by a white diamond contain consecutive digits. Not all possible white pellets have been given. ALL white pellets in the grid must be consumed along Snaake's path.
ᴱᵈᴵᵗᵒʳ'ˢ ᴺᵒᵗᵉ — ᵂʰᶦᵗᵉ ᵖᵉˡˡᵉᵗˢ ʷᶦˡˡ ᵃˡˢᵒ ʰᵉˡᵖ ᵗᵒ ᶜˡᵉᵃʳ ᵘᵖ ᵇᵃᵈ ᵇʳᵉᵃᵗʰ
BLACK PELLETS:
Digits separated by a black diamond have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other). Not all possible black pellets have been given. They do not need to be consumed.
ᴱᵈᴵᵗᵒʳ'ˢ ᴺᵒᵗᵉ — ᵀʰᵒᵘᵍʰ ᵗʰᵉʸ ᵐᵃʸ ᵇᵉ ᵃᵛᵒᶦᵈᵉᵈ ᵗʰᵉʸ ᵃʳᵉ ᵃᵇˢᵒˡᵘᵗᵉˡʸ ᵈᵉˡᶦᶜᶦᵒᵘˢ
TRIALS and TRAILS:
In this test of friendship, box borders and wormholes divide Snaake's path into segments. A segment total is calculated by summing its digits. For two segments that are visited adjacently along Snaake's path, their totals always have the same difference; to be deduced. Good luck!

title: Beware the Sliding Horses
description:
Here's where you can try Horses Sliding through a Field of Oil and Water by Merdock: https://sudokupad.app/bh7z9bwzxx
Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog may be cleared by correctly placed digits. Digits a knight's move away can not be identical. Digits in a cage cannot repeat. If a number is given in the upper left corner of the cage, then the digits in the cage must sum to that number. 
Each cage is either full of "oil" (even digits), full of "water" (odd digits), or a mix of both. In cases where cells of a cage are connected to each other horizontally, those cells must only contain one type (oil or water). If two cells are a part of the same cage and in the same row, but they are not connected horizontally (r5c6 & r5c8 for example), then they can be different types. Oil floats on water, so even digits will always be in rows above odd digits in mixed cages.

title: The Miracle Sudoku Of The Year!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon opens tonight's sudoku on camera! It's called Casino Royale, it's by Michael Lefkowitz and it'll take a moment or two to realise why Mark thought this would be a good one for a live unveil. Suffice it to say, this is an unbelievable idea/execution etc. Michael has made something very memorable with perhaps the greatest final line of rules ever! (There is also a musical outro today.)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/w51sf3oxio?setting-nogrid

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Place nine digits along the line. A digit X in position Y requires a digit Y in position X. (Position 1 being on the far left diamond, position 9 on the far right tip.) Digits on the line are skyscraper clues, i.e. they indicate how many digits in the column are larger than all digits lower down in the column. The grey area sums to an even total.

title: Setting The Record Straight
description:
Here's where you can try Setting Things Straight by Jrosas: https://sudokupad.app/4gausxmp2d 
Normals udoku rules apply. Yin Yang: The grid is divided into exactly two regions of orthogonally connected cells. No 2x2 square of cells is entirely in either region.
+/-1 lines: adjacent cells along a line share differ by 1 and share their yin Yang region. ALL possible lines are given.
Counting circles: There are 12 circles in the grid. A digit in a circle indicates how many circles contain that digit and a digit in a circle in a yin Yang region indicates how many cells in that yin Yang region contain the digit. ALL possible circles are given.
Dynamic fog. One cell is covered with fog. Correctly placing a digit in a particular cell will clear the fog.

And this was the other puzzle mentioned in the video: Leap Frog of War by Four by Jrosas: https://sudokupad.app/tuaw81xtfc 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Correctly placing a digit removes fog from the surrounding cells. Adjacent digits across a frog differ by exactly 4. All possible frogs are given.

title: Enter The (Foggy) Sudoku Mansion!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We haven't featured a Nurator puzzle for a while as he has been busy creating a new sudoku game called Sudoku Mansion (linked below). Tonight we attempt one of the sudokus from that game; it's called The Vault and it's absolutely epic. 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/mhfpkgyo52

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one digit is double the other. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Deducing the digit in a visible checkpoint (marked with a green square) will reveal new cells and potentially a new checkpoint.  Each line follows a specific constraint type from a list of constraints. It is up to the solver to determine which line belongs to which type.  Each line constraint type may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. At the start of the puzzle, all lines are German Whisper Lines (ie Adjacent digits differ by at least 5). Whenever new lines are revealed, remove all entered digits except those on checkpoints. After the first new lines are revealed, all lines can now be Region Sum Lines as well as Whispers. (ie The 3x3 box borders divide the lines into segments, each having the same sum). After the second new set of lines are revealed, the lines can now also be Modular lines (ie Every 3 consecutive cells along a modular line must contain a digit from (3,6,9), a digit from (1,4,7) and a digit from (2,5,8)). 

Sudoku Mansion, the new game from Nurator, is available here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/5005590/Sudoku_Mansion/

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along dashed orange lines must have a difference of 4 or more. Digits along solid purple lines form a consecutive set. Along a hollow peach line adjacent digits will be from different ‘entropic sets’, which are: low digits (1,2,3), medium digits (4,5,6) and high digits (7,8,9).
In each box containing a cage, sum all digits which are on two lines, and write that number into the cage. Two digit numbers must be entered left-to-right or top-to-bottom. The digit in the cell with the green square is equal to the sum of all of the tens digits from every two digit number. The digit in the cell with the blue circle is equal to the sum of all of the units digits from every two digit number.

title: The Invisible Sudoku Thermometers
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A strange and wondrous sudoku tonight from Vythic called Dual Summits. We didn't know a great deal about it before Simon tried it: A couple of (very strong) recommendations and one tester saying it was great but it is well worth your puzzle time. A very unusual and interesting idea with a lot of new logic to get your head around! Fabulous!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/0o34f0060w

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a blue line are ascending or descending, with 1 and 9 reversing the ascension/descension. Every possible sequence along a blue line must obey this rule. There are exactly two blue lines in the grid, which are mostly hidden. All visible blue line pieces in the grid contain a tip (end) of a blue line; all tips are visible. No blue line travels through an entire 2x2 cluster of cells. Blue lines must travel orthogonally, and CAN branch out. Every digit in the grid is on a blue line except for digits in a cage. Cells separated by a white dot contain separate blue lines. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. A thermometer shares cells with only one blue line. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb to the tip. Digits in a cage sum to the number in the top left of the cage (and are not on a blue line).

*** BRAND NEW COMPETITION ON PATREON ***
On 1 Septmber we released a new Sudoku Hunt competition on Patreon. There's 8 puzzles to solve by 20 September to win the chance to come onto the channel and solve a puzzle with us! title: Do NOT Try Doing Sudoku In This 9x9 Grid!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears can always be relied upon for a brilliant puzzle and tonight we attempt another of his Isofills (like a sudoku but not). It may be a 9x9 grid and involve the digits 1-9 but don't try and do sudoku with this one!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/70njbfg1zs

Rules
Divide the grid into 9 regions, each containing 9 orthogonally connected cells. All cells in the same region must contain the same digit. All of the digits 1-9 must appear in the grid. Each peach line must contain one low digit (1, 2 or 3), one medium digit (4, 5 or 6) and one high digit (7, 8 or 9.) Digits along a thermometer must keep increasing as they move from bulb to tip.

title: A Sudoku Results In Mexican Standoff!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What a sudoku this is. Starwarigami returns to the setting scene tonight with a phenomenal 5/5 difficulty puzzle which is a total delight from start to finish. The logic is original, clever and quite wonderful here.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/db1522df7f

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Fully colour the grid with three colours A, B, and C, such that each cage is completely filled with only one colour, all cells of the same colour are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area of the grid is completely filled by one colour. The colour of certain cells has been given. Digits may not repeat in a cage, and each cage sums to a unique total. Cages marked with a letter in the top left corner sum to the number of squares in the grid filled with that colour. Cages filled with the same colour all have the same remainder when divided by 3.

title: Sudoku's Rat Runs Return!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A couple of weeks ago we solved the first puzzle, Feeding Friendsy by Marty Sears, in a series of Rat Run-inspired sudokus made for Marty by his friends! The second such puzzle (It's Not Pea-sy Being Green by sujoyku) was actually solved by Mark about a year ago! Tonight Simon tries the third: Lettuce Experiment by Ratfinkz. The biggest compliment we can pay Ratfinkz is that this FELT like a Rat Run!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/vdnlyzrag0

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply.

#FRIENDSHIPGOALS:
Prof Sears has been immersing himself in a lot of mad science lately, and frankly has been neglecting his own health. Time for him to try a vegetable instead... he must find his way through the lab to reach his super-lettuce - genetically modified for extra minerals and nutrients. His path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, he may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall.

ONE-WAY DOORS: 
Prof Sears may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between.

TEST TUBES:
Digits separated by a test tube have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other).

TRIALS and TRAILS:
In this mission, Prof Sears's path is divided into segments by box borders (if he enters a box more than once, each instance counts as a new segment.) Each segment is a hitline, with the first cell visited on the segment being position 1. Any cell that equals its position number along its segment is a HITPOINT (eg: if the 2nd digit visited along a segment is a 2.) The HIT TOTAL of a segment equals the sum of its hitpoints. (Eg: a segment reading 127854 would have a hit total of 8; the sum of 1, 2 and 5, which are the only digits in their correct position.) Every clipboard must display the hit total for each and every segment in its 3x3 box (and each box contains at least one segment).  Eg: if a clipboard reads 7, then any and all path segments in its box each individually have a HIT TOTAL of 7.

title: Searching Everywhere in the Grid!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Searching High & Low by Daniel Hanson: https://sudokupad.app/6ukcd457re 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. A cell marked as a MAX cell (wedges pointing outward) is larger than all orthogonal and diagonal neighbours; a cell marked as a MIN cell (wedges pointing inward) is smaller than all orthogonal and diagonal neighbours. All possible MAX and MIN cells are shown. Cells marked with a cage are either BIG or SMALL; a BIG/SMALL cell is larger/smaller than its orthogonal neighbors but is not larger/smaller than at least one diagonal neighbour. (In other words, a BIG/SMALL cell cannot be a MAX/MIN cell.) All possible BIG and SMALL cells are shown. Whether a marked cell is BIG or SMALL must be determined by the solver. Somewhere in the grid is a single magic square made from nine distinct digits arranged in a square such that every row, column, and diagonal of the square sum to the same total.

title: The Hardest Puzzle We've Ever Attempted? Perhaps!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Dozens and dozens of you have requested we attempt tonight's puzzle, the last of the Lupin's Loop series by Rab3aron, Lupin's Loop 7: Where It All Began. The comments seem to agree on two things: 1) this is masterpiece; 2) this is brutally difficult. We can confirm on both counts!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/p676oglsv8

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Divide the grid into four distinct regions. Each region consists of orthogonally connected cells and touches each of the other three regions orthogonally too (ie shares at least one edge). No 2×2 block may be entirely within one region. At least two regions are the same size. 
Draw two distinct orthogonally connected, non-branching paths, each joining a pair of hourglasses determined by the solver. The paths share exactly one cell, marked by the red pin, and otherwise do not overlap. Along one path, adjacent digits have opposite parity, along the other, adjacent digits are consecutive. 
A digit in an hourglass equals the number of times its path crosses the border of the region containing that hourglass. A digit N in a purple Sensor means the digit N appears exactly N times within that sensor’s region. Neither path may pass through a blue dot. Digits in cells joined by a green dot differ by at least 5. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive. If two digits are joined by a black dot one is TRIPLE the other. Digits in a cage sum to the value in its top-left corner and do not repeat within a cage. 
A digit in a cell with arrows equals the total number of cells containing any part of either path in all indicated directions, including the clue cell itself.
Numbers outside the grid on a diagonal indicate the sum of the first X cells along that diagonal. The value of X is not 6 and must be determined by the solver. 
A number N outside a row/column means the first N cells from that side are in the same region, and the (N+1)th cell is in a different region.

Note: You may finish one part before the others (digits, paths, and regions), but the puzzle is only solved once all three parts are completed.

description:
Here's where you can try The Ant(i) Farm by HDev: https://sudokupad.app/3yyqe1we8y 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent cells directly connected by a visible (brown) tunnel segment must have a ratio of exactly 2, 3, or 4.
Any orthogonally adjacent cells that are not directly connected by a visible tunnel segment can never have a ratio of 2, 3, or 4. For example, although R4C1 and R5C1 both have visible tunnel segments connecting them to other cells, they are not directly connected by a tunnel segment and therefore cannot have a ratio of 2, 3, or 4.
All visible tunnel segments are shown.
The two diagonals originating from the red circle have equal sums. The two diagonals originating from the green circle also have equal sums.

title: An Extraordinary Sudoku Debut
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An amazing debut on the channel tonight for Varepsilon and their sudoku, Out Of Touch. It features an original ruleset and feels like lots of puzzles in one. Not easy but fun and interesting from start to finish!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/y0rmb0d1m1

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Draw a single closed loop that moves orthogonally through cell centers. It must leave exactly nine cells unvisited and visit every other cell exactly once. 
The nine unvisited cells contain 1–9 once each, with no two unvisited cells in the same row, column, or 3x3 box. If a cell contains a digit equal to its position within its box then that cell IS unvisited. (Box positions are numbered in normal reading order so the top left cell is position 1 and the bottom right cell is position 9). If a cell does not contain its position within its box then it IS visited. 
The loop can be divided into nine consecutive 8-cell sections, each containing eight different digits. The unvisited cell containing a section's missing digit may not share an edge with any cell in that section.

description:
Here's where you can try Group Theory by Gabriel Kammer: https://sudokupad.app/q66okox4du 
You have been gifted a large collection of puzzles from a friend. You sift through them looking for interesting ones and find a photocopy of a puzzle from an old book of puzzles. Normal sudoku rules apply.
Digits along a purple Renban line form a set of consecutive digits in any order.
Adjacent digits along a green German Whispers line have a difference of at least 5.

description:
*** BRAND NEW COMPETITION ON PATREON ***

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. If two digits are joined by a black dot, one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a white dot, they are consecutive. Digits on a pink line form a non-repeating, conseuctive sequence which can be arranged in any order along the line. Box borders divide a blue line into segments, each of which have the same sum. Digits along a grey thermometer must increase as they get further away from the bulb. On a red line, digits must alternate between even and odd. title: Can A Sudoku Teach You Interesting Maths?
description:
*** BRAND NEW COMPETITION ON PATREON ***
Yesterday afternoon we released a new Sudoku Hunt competition on Patreon. There's 8 puzzles to solve by 20 September to win the chance to come onto the channel and solve a puzzle with us! 

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It is hard to overstate how fascinating tonight's sudoku was to Simon. It's called Base 2 and it's the work of Hanks, a new constructor to the channel. Without giving anything away, we'll be very interested to read the comments on this one and discover just how obvious some of what's happening is!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/dnz6khw1tf

Rules
Fill the grid with the digits 0-8 such that every row, column, and 3x3 box contains each digit exactly once. The value of a cell equals 2 to the power of N, where N is the digit in the cell. Note that 2 to the power of 0 equals 1. Values of cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. If two cells are separated by a black dot then one cells' value is double the other. Values of cells separated by an X sum to 10. Values of cells separated by a V sum to 5. Values of cells on an arrow MAY repeat, and must sum to the value of the cell containing the attached circle. Values of adjacent cells on a green line have a difference of at least 5. The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments. The sum of values of cells on each segment is the same. (The sum may be different for different blue lines). Values of cells in a cage MAY repeat, and must sum to the given cage total in the leftmost cell of the topmost row of the cage. Entering a correct digit clears fog in its cell, and may or may not clear fog in other cells.

title: An Absolutely Incredible Sudoku Feat
description:
Here's where you can try Querulous by Nicolas Duhail: https://sudokupad.app/2jar2lhcc5 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move cannot contain the same digit. All lines sum to the same total.
Any three adjacent digits along the teal "modular" line have different residues modulo 3 (i.e. one digit from {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8}, and one from {3,6,9}). Box borders divide the blue "region sum" line into segments with the same sum. Along the pink "renban" line, digits form a consecutive sequence in any order. Along the orange "dutch whisper" line, adjacent digits differ by at least 4. Along the gold "nabner" line, digits do not repeat and no two digits appearing anywhere on the line can be consecutive. Any three adjacent digits along the peach "entropic" line contains one low digit (123), one middle digit (456), and one high digit (789). Along the green "german whisper" line, adjacent digits differ by at least 5. Digits along the red "parity" line must alternate between odd and even.

title: Sorry Sudoku Solver Tries To Make Amends
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely lovely sudoku tonight from Ratfinkz (recommended by Marty Sears no less) called Every Hit Counts. The introduction to the video also includes Simon going over some of yesterday's logic in IcyFruit's Diamondback puzzle for those of you who were understandably upset during his solve thereof.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/gfx29v36nv

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Beige lines are "hit point lines": Counting the diamond as position one, digits in their correct position must sum to the number in the diamond (eg a line who's diamond was the value 9 may be made up 93145 as 4&5 are in the 4th and 5th position and sum to 9 fulfilling the diamonds requirements). Digits may not repeat along a line (the digit in the diamond is considered on the line and may not appear elsewhere along its line). Digits in the diamonds also count how many different lines they appear on, including themselves (eg if a diamond contained the number  3 it would appear,  in any position, on two more lines). Digits which don't appear in a diamond have no limitations as to how many lines they appear on.

Tonight's sudoku, .357 Magnum by Eric Rathbun, is almost unbelievably clever. There are moments of genuine astonishment during the solve of this one... for Simon's money, this is a stone cold classic.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/r9hx4s0yib

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the cage's top left corner. The clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits cannot repeat along the main diagonal marked with a blue line. The grey square contains an even digit. Grey lines are palindromes ie they read the same forwards and backwards. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of one. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one is double the

title: What's the Point of a Pulsar?
description:
Here's where you can attempt Pointers and Pulsars by David Sadler: https://sudokupad.app/2a25cs6i6d 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Some cells contain a diagonal marker indicating one of the two diagonal directions (NW–SE or NE–SW). For each such cell, consider the two cells located exactly two steps away along that diagonal. The value in the marked cell equals the value in the cell two steps downward, raised to the power of the value in the cell two steps upward.
Some cells contain arrows pointing to one or more adjacent cells. The value in each such cell equals the arithmetic mean of the values in all cells it points to.

title: Wait, That Looks Like A "Rat Run" Sudoku?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears introduces us to a new series of puzzles, most of which are by his friends and all of which are themed on his own 'Rat Run' style of sudokus (which you can watch all 40 or so episodes of on our special playlist!) These puzzles will be released every Wednesday but Marty introduces the series with his one tonight called Feeding Friendsy - a spectacular and beautiful way to spend a Friday evening!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/l50613nsxb

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. 

Nine unlikely friends must each find a path through their box, to reach something that will give them an energy boost.

FEEDING MISSIONS:
• BOX 1: The frog must reach the fly resting on a waterlily.
• BOX 2: The mad scientist must reach his lettuce.
• BOX 3: The digital snake must reach the cake.
• BOX 4: The robot must reach the battery.
• BOX 5: The dolphin must reach the fish.
• BOX 6: The flamingo must reach the pancakes.
• BOX 7: The cat must reach the milk.
• BOX 8: The zebra must reach the broccoli.
• BOX 9: The hippo must reach the doughnut.

MOVEMENT:
Characters each stay in their own box, but do not necessarily need to visit all 9 cells. They may not pass through any thick walls, visit any cell more than once, or cross their own paths. As well as moving orthogonally, they may also move diagonally if there is a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass through the end of a wall on the corner of a cell.

MATCHING PATHS: Every character visits exactly the same sequence of digits, in the same order.

ONE WAY DOORS: A purple arrow points towards the smaller of the two digits it sits between, and may only be passed through in the direction it's pointing.

EXTRA ITEMS: If two digits are separated by a test tube (in box 2), a metal gear (in box 4), a black sea urchin (in box 5), or a cookie (in box 7),  then one digit is double the other. Extra items may or may not be visited.

title: Utter Cubic Chaos
description:
Here's where you can attempt Cube Chaos by Mellowrobinson: https://sudokupad.app/odyy7oejuu 
The grid is a 4x4x4 cube. The layers are stacked as shown by the dashed lines (without rotation). Fill every cell with a digit from 1-8 so digits don't repeat in the x, y, or z axis.
Divide the grid into eight orthogonally connected regions, each containing the digits 1-8 without repeats.
The digit in a circle counts the number of cells of its own region that it 'sees' in all three directions, including itself, where other regions and the edge of the cube blocks vision. A number clue indicates the sum of such seen cells, if given.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
You would think that Simon would be well prepared to deal with a new Isofill collaboration between sujoyku and Marty Sears after he did the prequel to this puzzle a couple of weeks ago... https://sudokupad.app/u5hbzubozt

Rules:
Divide the grid into 10 regions, each with 10 orthogonally connected cells. Every cell in a region should contain the same digit. All of the digits 0-9 must appear in the grid. No two digits on a yellow line may be the same or consecutive. The two digits at either end of a lavender line sum to the digit on the central spot.

title: Only 10 People Have EVER Solved This Puzzle. Can He Make It 11?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon is a massive fan of Kaktuslav's sudokus and he's been waiting for a big chunk of spare time to attempt this must-requested puzzle by the great man. It's called Blue Cages and only 10 people have managed to finish it... 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9xec41tr2z

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine non-overlapping regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Some borders between the regions are already given. Fill the grid with digits 1–9 so that each row, column, and region contains each digit exactly once. Digits may not repeat within a cage, and no cage is entirely contained within a single region. Region borders divide each cage into pieces with equal sums. That is, in each region containing cells of a cage, those cells form a single orthogonally connected piece, and all pieces of that cage have the same sum (different cages may have different sums). Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots are necessarily given.
