title: This Is ACTUALLY A Miracle Sudoku.
description:
▶ TONIGHT'S STREAM: LORELEI AND THE LASER EYES ◀ 
You can watch tonight's stream of Lorelei and the Laser Eyes at 10pm on here:

https://youtube.com/live/4x48s0DGAIM

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears does incredible things in sudoku grids. This puzzle, Galaxies Collide (Again!), is one of his finest hours. The number of beautiful logical steps necessary to solve it is exceptional but so is the fact that this grid can possibly exist. How in the galaxy can this have a unique solution? You'll see what we mean if you give it a try.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yporyghx5a

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into two galaxies of orthogonally connected cells. No 2x2 area may be completely within one galaxy. Both galaxies must be symmetrical through 180 degrees. A digit in a green circle indicates how many cells in its sudoku box are in its galaxy. A digit in a red square indicates how many cells in its sudoku box are NOT in its galaxy. One of the two galaxies is special. In that galaxy, for any two orthogonally adjacent cells, dividing one digit by the other always gives an exact integer (one is a multiple of the other.)

title: How is this Even Possible?
description:
Here's where you can try Even Regions by Vythic: https://sudokupad.app/gaonp82fme 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are four hidden Even Regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells containing even digits. Orthogonally adjacent even digits always belong to the same Even Region. A digit on an arrow indicates how many digits of the opposite parity are in the direction of the arrow. (ie if the digit is even, it counts odd digits, and vice versa). If a cell has multiple arrows, count each direction independently.
On a black dot, one digit is double the other. On a white dot, digits are consecutive. Digits in a cage sum to the number in the top-left of the cage and cannot repeat.

title: How Easy Is This Little Puzzle?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
James Sinclair is a master sudoku constructor who can create great puzzles at any level of difficulty. Tonight we try Irwell, a 6x6, with the reputation for being quite approachable. How easy will you find it?!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/irwell

Rules:
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Exactly one cell in each row, column, and box is a "doubler", and doubler cells contain a complete set of the digits 1-6. The value of a doubler cell is equal to its digit multiplied by two. Values along thermometers increase from the bulb. Values in cells with a shaded square are even.

Find more puzzles like this at James' website: artisanalsudoku.com

title: The Most Requested Puzzle In Years: Lupin's Loop 6
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We have been receiving so many requests to attempt the next puzzle in Rab3aron's Lupin's Loop series. It's clearly a very difficult sudoku so Simon has been waiting for a reasonably chunky window of time to attempt it... Tonight's the night!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9snrpdy9fe

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a yellow dot are non-consecutive. Digits separated by a red dot must contain one even digit and one odd digit. Draw a single cable that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branches, crosses, or overlaps itself, and eventually closes into a loop. The cable must pass through every electricity sign and may not cross rivers (blue borders). 90-degree turns split the loop into segments (including endpoints). If a segment of length N exists, then the total number of segments of length N in the loop is M, where M is greater than 1 and M and N share the same parity. Additionally, if a segment has length N, then the digit N must appear in one of that segment’s endpoints. A digit in a purple sensor counts the number of loop cells in the 3×3 box centered on that sensor, up to a maximum of 9. Cells on the marked diagonals may not be part of any segment of length exactly 5.

title: Around The World In 80 Days: The Fog(g) Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
How has no-one had this idea before! Liam McG's first ever puzzle combines the wonderful novel by Jules Verne with fog sudoku. Will Phileas Fogg win his bet with the Reform club and make it home in 80 days. [The version below has a slight ruleset tweak to the version Simon attempts in the video.]

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/wq1p4nwud6

Rules:
London, 1872. Phileas Fogg wagers a fortune that he can circumnavigate the globe in just eighty days. Unbeknownst to him, a detective named Fix, convinced Fogg is really a bank robber fleeing the country, has resolved to stop him. Will he be successful? Discover Fogg's route around the globe and tally the days to find out.

RULES
Normal sudoku rules apply.

'Fogg' of War: The grid starts partially obscured with fog. Placing enough digits correctly will lift fog from an adjacent box.

White Kropki Dots: Cells with a white-dot are consecutive. All white dots are given. 

Killer Cages:  If a cage has a number in its top-left cell, digits in that cage sum to it.

Detective Fix: In 3x3 box n, Fix is disguised as digit n. Fix cannot be in a cage but must be orthogonally adjacent to a cage or cages in the same box. Boxes are numbered in normal reading order.

Path (around the world): Draw a orthogonally connected path to form a loop which visits every box at least once and never forms a 2×2 block. Across the whole loop, the path passes through exactly one Fix cell and exactly one cage cell — they need not be in the same box. Additionally, every cell with a white (Kropki) dot is on the path, though not all path cells need a white dot.

Total Days: Digits on the loop count the days of Fogg's journey. The sum of these digits will therefore show whether Fogg succeeds in circumnavigating the globe in 80 days. Note: you should not assume the sum is 80 — or any other total — for he might not make it in time... that is for you to find out!

Crossing the International Date Line: Any digit in a cell in which the path actually crosses (ie not just touches) the red International Date line does not count toward the sum (to account for crossing the International Date Line!).

title: Sudoku in the Sweet Spot
description:
Here's where you can try Hitting the Sweet Spot by PrissyP: https://sudokupad.app/tgewrz1n8q 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Find a Sweet Spot cell on every line such that the cell divides the line into two hitlines. The digit in the Sweet Spot has two meanings: It equals the NUMBER of hits on one hitline; It equals the SUM of the hit digits on the other hitline. Either hitline may take either role.
A hit is a digit that matches its distance from the Sweet Spot, counting outward from it. The cell adjacent to the Sweet Spot is at distance 1, the next cell is at distance 2, and so on. Digits may NOT repeat within a hitline. Example: In 7694321(6)1235, the Sweet Spot is the digit 6. On the left hitline there are 6 hits, while on the right the hit digits are 1, 2, and 3, whose sum is 6, so the line satisfies the rule.

title: One Of The CLEVEREST Puzzles Of The Year.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Continuing to catch up with puzzles recommended during his holidays last month, Simon tackles Summetry by Kaktuslav this evening. Some of you have suggested this is a candidate for Puzzle Of The Year - and it totally is.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/o4u3kz1764

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2×2 region is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. The shading must also be centrally symmetric: cells mapped to each other by a 180∘ rotation about the center of the grid have the same shading. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Each cage contains at least one shaded and one unshaded cell, and the sum of its unshaded digits equals the product of its shaded digits (a sum or product consisting of a single digit is simply that digit).

title: What do you Mean you want Fractions? In Sudoku?
description:
Here's where you can try Ground Floor by Ishie: https://sudokupad.app/88frf3hrkd 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every cell has a numerical value greater than 0 and less than 10.
The value of a cell marked with a brown ╚═══╝ is always non-integer and its digit is its value rounded down to the nearest integer. The value of a cell marked with a pink ╔══╗ is always non-integer and its digit is its value rounded up to the nearest integer. All other cells must have an integer value and its digit matches its value.
On a black dot, one cell value is double the other. On a teal diamond, one cell value is triple the other Adjacent cells along green German whispers lines have values that differ by at least 5. Values along an arrow sum to the value in the attached circle.

title: That's No Sudoku! It's A "Marty Sears" Puzzle!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears is a sudoku genius. But this is no sudoku!! It turns out he's a genius at making puzzles too. This one is called Homogenous - because every cell in a region must be the same digit. Welcome to the strange new world of Isofill!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/0htle6wxey

Rules:
Divide the grid into 10 regions, each with 10 orthogonally connected cells. Every cell in a region should contain the same digit. All of the digits 0-9 must appear in the grid. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. If a black dot sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a green dot sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5.

title: Do Not Always Be Anti Knight!
description:
Here's where you can try Anti & Pro Knights by Eric Bader: https://sudokupad.app/n837muu8j6 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the number shown. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. A pink line contains a consecutive group of digits in any order without repeats. Each digit 9 must not be a chess knight’s move away from another 9. Each digit 1 must be a chess knights move away from at least TWO different 1s. All knight’s moves see the grid cylindrically/as a torus, for example R1C2 would see R2C9, R8C1, R8C3, and R9C4  wrapping around the grid; as well as normal knight’s moves like R2C4.

title: A Quite Astonishing Fog-Of-War Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Some of you have recommended tonight's sudoku using words like "masterpiece"... it's called Consecutive Regional Constraints and it's by Belamis. It features a twist on one of Simon's favourite rules (where you cannot repeat a digit on a constraint) and this leads to some crazy logic. Read the rules carefully, don't guess and let us know how you get on!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/zt3l4bqwuj

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Correctly placed digits may remove fog from other cells. 
Any constraint type can not have a repeated digit. (E.g. if a 2 appears on a parity line, another 2 may not appear on any parity line.) In addition, digits across a constraint type must make up a consecutive set of digits. (E.g. if a 2 and 4 exist on dutch whisper line(s), there must also be a 3 somewhere on a dutch whisper line.) 
Constraint types: 
1. Arrow - Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the connected circle. Each circle is associated with exactly one arrow; 
2. Region Sum (RS) - The 3x3 box borders divide a blue line into segments;  each segment along an individual line must have the same sum. Each line crosses at least 1 box border and does not branch;
3. Renban (R) - Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order; 
4. Dutch Whispers (DW) - Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least 4; 
5. Entropic (E) - Any three adjacent digits along a peach line are from one each of low(1,2,3), medium(4,5,6), and high(7,8,9) digits. Entropic lines must be at least 3 cells long; 
6. Kropki - Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive; 
7. Parity (P) - Along a red line, adjacent digits must alternate between odd and even.

title: An EPIC "Blue Prince" Sudoku Attempted
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the most unusual and, frankly, brilliant sudokus you'll ever find tonight from Sudoku Joker. It's called Drafting Strategy and it is a paean to the popular video game, Blue Prince. Only this version of the game is quite hard - at least that's what Simon thinks!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/qbx29s7dud

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, no cell may be double the value of any orthogonally adjacent cell. The central 5x9 area of the grid depicts a floorplan of a house, with openings between cells representing doorways between rooms. There is one way that this house can be traversed visiting each room only once, starting from the cell marked "E" (the house's Entrance Hall) and ending in the cell marked "A" (the antechamber). You start with 50 footsteps. Every time you enter a purple room, you gain 10 steps, and every time you enter a red room, your total number of steps is halved. Every time you enter any other type of room, you lose 1 step. Your step count is always a whole number and may not fall to zero at any time during the walk through the house. The path travelled through the house forms a region sum line: Region sum lines are divided by the 3x3 sudoku box borders into sections which each have the same sum. Digits in two adjacent green rooms sum to 10. A digit in a purple room is smaller than any of the digits in orthogonally adjacent cells. Two rooms of the same colour may not contain the same digit.

title: A Polo Field with Tumbleweed?
description:
Here's where you can attempt poLo by Mattisahuman: https://sudokupad.app/w3ve69np9y 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Red cells with outward pointing arrows are larger than all of their orthogonal neighbors. Blue cells with inward pointing arrows are smaller than all of their orthogonal neighbors.
Draw a loop into the grid that may only move orthogonally and may not touch itself, not even diagonally. Additionally, fortress cells are never part of the loop; however, all fortress cells touch the loop either orthogonally or diagonally (or both). The loop is broken up into segments by box borders. These segments are index lines which are all oriented in the same direction about the loop, to be determined by the solver.
Index Lines: The digit in the Nth cell along a segment indicates the position along the segment where the digit N appears. For example: 2143 would be a valid segment; the 1st digit, 2, indicates that the 2nd digit is a 1, and so on.

title: Watch Out, Weasel!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Pop Goes The World by Alchemist: https://sudokupad.app/m1p2mis3fb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Place one trigger cell in each row, column and 3 by 3 box. Each of these trigger cells is a ‘popped’ cell. All cells orthogonally adjacent to a popped cell also pop if they have a smaller digit than (any of) the adjacent popped cell(s). Continue until no more cells pop. 
Bubbles (circles) are never in cells which are popped and count the number of (up to 8, including diagonals) surrounding cells which are popped. Pinpricks (inequalities) ‘point’ to the smaller of the two digits they separate, and always separate a cell which has been popped from a cell which hasn't.

title: This Incredible New Type Of Sudoku Has Everything!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for the constructor Jekyll and their puzzle Slide-oku: Penguindrome, which features an incredibly clever new ruleset involving sliding over the grid's ice. We think this video has a lot of things in it: drama, story-telling, a touch of logic, madness, mistakes and catharsis. All in 90 minutes or so... do you agree!?

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ebemk89tg1

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a path from the penguin to the shrimp. The ground is covered in turquoise slippery ice. When the penguin starts sliding in a direction it can not stop until it hits an obstacle (a wall or a rock) and stops in the preceding cell. The path can then turn in any available orthogonal direction and continue until the next obstacle. The path can cross itself but not overlap. All coins that are collected along the penguin's path are BLACK KROPKI dots (ie one digit will be double the other). All coins that are not on the penguin's path are WHITE KROPKI dots (digits separated by the dot are consecutive). Not all possible coins are shown. In this puzzle, the penguin's path is a valid PALINDROME LINE (digits along the line read the same in both directions).

title: The Fog And The Phistomefel = Sudoku Genius
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Oh my goodness tonight's sudoku is a Worldie from Rosie called Feeling Rough. One look at the grid will hint at what's going on but figuring out how to actually enter anything is another challenge altogether. This is REALLY REALLY good.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/nmzsv3jbx9

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing a correct digit might clear some of the fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is required. A digit in a circle indicates roughly how many circles contain that digit i.e. X in a circle indicates that X appears in either X+1 or X-1 circles (but not in exactly X circles). All circles are visible i.e. no circles are hidden behind fog. Orthogonally adjacent circles must have different entropy i.e. a digit from a different set {1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}, or {7, 8, 9}. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle.

Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog will clear for correct digits. There are 2 types of cages...you have to figure out which ones are which. In a killer cage, the digits sum to the numbers in the top corner of the cage. Numbers cannot repeat in such a cage. In a Look-and-say cage, read the clues out loud, e.g. 22 says there are “two two(s)” in the cage.
On a black dot, one digit is double the other. On a white dot, digits are consecutive. Adjacent cells on a green line differ by at least 5. Cells on a grey sequence line must be the same amount apart and in order. E.g. 111 456 2468 741 9753.

title: Is This 5x5 Sudoku Even Remotely Difficult?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Dorlir, the maths professor, has set tonight's puzzle: Supersquish Dominoes. It's such a simple concept and, according to its rating, not so difficult... and yet...!!! So original and very very clever... Let us know what you think.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/dgpf3zkpjp

Rules:

title: The Miracle Sudoku Loop
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A rarity on the channel today: Simon returns from his holidays to find a mountain of recommended puzzles to try and the first one up is by the same author as yesterday, Marty Sears! Simon needs no persuasion to do another of Marty's sudokus and this one is extraordinary. How can only these five cell markings completely specify a unique grid...? Let's see...

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/dk7jgt7xov

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a loop, one-cell wide, that moves orthogonally between cells. The loop cannot touch itself, even diagonally: ie If two loop cells are side-by-side, they must be directly connected by the loop; and, if a 2×2 area contains two diagonal loop cells, they must be connected by a third loop cell in that same 2x2. A green circle is on the loop, and its digit indicates the number of cells in its box that are on the loop. A red square is NOT on the loop, and its digit indicates the number of cells in its box that are NOT on the loop. For any two neighbouring cells along the loop, dividing one by the other gives an exact integer (one is a multiple of the other.)

title: Make Sure This Has Exactly TWO Solutions!?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A very original and different sudoku tonight from JT called Schrödinger... the idea is that, when you've finished, every instance of two digits can be switched and the puzzle must still "work"! It's a debut for JT and a REALLY good one...  Enjoy!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/4jjr2ooiit

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. In this puzzle, there exists a pair of digits where, if you were to swap all the final positions of the two digits in the finished grid, the puzzle would still reach a solution which satisfies the conditions set by all other clues. The special pair of digits (the swappable digit pair) is two distinct digits which add to 10. The swappable digit pair is a discoverable, persistent and necessary component for solving this puzzle.

title: If You Have A Brain The Size Of A Planet...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

...then you can make this puzzle. Andrewsarchus is the person responsible for this incredible sudoku; it's called Congruity and it will almost certainly break your brain! Perhaps the ultimate "indexing" sudoku!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/0olvm9qcyz

Rules
Place digits 1-9 once each into each row and column of the bold outlined 9x9 grid. The blue lines are Index Lines. The value in the Nth cell along an Index Line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the value N appears. For example, if a diamond cell contains a 3, the third cell along that line must have a 1. The lavender lines are Zipper Lines: Pairs of values equidistant from the centre of a Zipper Line have the same sum (S). The centre (marked with a circle) contains that sum ie the value S. The sum may be different for different lines. A value in an external cell represents the rank of the number formed by reading the digits in that row or column from that direction, where (1) is the lowest such row or column and (36) is the highest. (The 36 numbers are distinct - no ties).

title: 100%-Rated Sudokus Are Pretty Clever!!
description:
We have made it to 700,000 Subscribers! THANK YOU SO MUCH

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight we continue our journey through Rab3aron's Lupin's Loop sudoku series with episode 5: Countercount. As well as testing your flag knowledge (at which Simon fails!), you'll find a puzzle that will intrigue and delight in equal measure. This is absolutely worth its perfect rating - a totally stunning construction and a joy to solve.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ybaev4x39i

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. A greater than sign points to the smaller number. Draw a single route for the airplane that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, and eventually closing into a loop. The route starts at the airplane, passes through every country, and returns to its starting point. Thick black borders represent heavy turbulence that the airplane cannot cross. If a digit N appears on the route, then the digit N appears exactly N times in cells not on the route. If two countries are directly connected by the route, their digits differ by the length of the segment connecting them. If a country and the airplane are directly connected by the route, the digit in the airplane equals the length of the segment connecting them. Note: Segment lengths include both endpoints. Two objects are directly connected by the route if no other object lies between them along the route.

title: Danger! Emergency! Sudoku!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Unlucky 13 by Possible Spam Risk: https://sudokupad.app/4b16rwzym1 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that sum to the number in the square and are shaded the color of the clue. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color. All runs are given. For many clues, the run’s sum is unknown. If the clue contains a single question mark, the clue is a one-digit number. If the clue contains two question marks, the clue is a two-digit number.
There are 13 three-digit emergency or crisis numbers represented by the listed clues. Every clue with a printed numeric value is part of one of these numbers; no unknown clue (? or ??) is part of any number. Each number is formed by reading clue values in order. For example, the number 615 could appear as a 6 followed by a 15. Identifying the actual emergency or crisis numbers is not necessary to solve the puzzle.

title: Rapunzel... Let Down Your "Sausage"??!
description:
We have made it to 700,000 Subscribers! THANK YOU SO MUCH

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A little while ago, we solved a puzzle by Scojo on the channel which looked almost identical to this one - it was called Rapuzzle and was one of the most popular sudokus of recent times. Tonight we attempt a "tribute" to that puzzle from ThePedallingPianist called Rapuzzle, Rapuzzle, Let Down Your Sausage. It would be easy to find this title extremely suggestive and/or funny. In truth this is actually a superb puzzle in its own right and it's frankly ridiculous that it's somehow been achieved while looking almost identical to its progenitor!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/wxbluqtoso

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
Tower Fortress: Cells that are part of the gray tower must be greater than all orthogonally adjacent non-tower cells. Note: any cell that the tower even partially covers is considered a fortress cell.
Rapunzel's Sausage: The difference between the sums of two linked sausages on a chain must be exactly equal to the number of sausages in that chain.
Rapunzel's Face: The digit on Rapunzel's face shows how many numbers of the opposite odd/even parity to itself appear on the whole sausage chain.

(Artwork by DubiousMobius; puzzle heavily inspired by Scojo)

title: The Miracle "Zipper" Sudoku
description:
We have made it to 700,000 Subscribers! THANK YOU SO MUCH

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A fabulous return from the maths professor Dorlir to the channel tonight and his puzzle Chaotic Zippers. It's scarcely creditable that, with so little information given, this puzzle solves - especially as the solver also has to build the regions... and yet it does! It's also not too difficult. Give yourself a few minutes of pleasure and solve this one!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/6k7r2bex5r

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally-connected cells. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9, once each. Zipper lines: Digits an equal distance from the centre of the purple line must sum to the digit in the centre of that purple line. Different zippers don't share cells with each other. The digit in the centre of a purple line counts how many regions contain at least one cell on that purple line. Some region borders are given. Entering a correct digit clears fog in its cell, and may or may not clear fog in other cells. No guessing is necessary.

title: The Rat And Cupcake Are Invisible!! Marty's Incredible Sudoku Snake
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Where to start on this incredible sudoku from Marty Sears. It has many of the hallmarks of his Rat Run series (but with no actual rat or cupcake). The whole thing has been SO well conceived and executed that it's scarcely credible. One of Simon's favourite puzzles of recent times.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/bq3bqqtcix

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
SNAKE:
Draw a snake, one cell wide, that starts and ends at two neighbouring cells within the same 3x3 box. The snake only moves orthogonally, and visits every cell in the grid apart from the large grey rock in the central cell. The snake may not enter any cell more than once.
INSECTS:
The snake must eat every insect, and these divide the snake into segments. Adjacent segments along the snake have consecutive totals. No two segments have the same total.
GREY PEBBLES:
The snake must not pass directly through any grey pebbles. Digits joined by a grey pebble are either consecutive, or have a 1:2 ratio (so one digit would be double the other).
EGGS:
One of the four digits surrounding an egg indicates the number of spots on that egg.

title: Win the Yellow Jersey
description:
Here's where you can try TDF: The Route by Palpot: https://sudokupad.app/7d9f9mb2y3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide path through the centers of cells, starting at the rider (R1C9) and ending at the medal (R3C5). The path moves orthogonally between cells. It may not branch or visit any cell more than once. Every set of three consecutive digits along the path must contain a low (1,2,3), a medium (4,5,6), and a high digit (7,8,9). 
Each mountain cell lies on the path. The path must travel straight vertically through each mountain cell. If the digit in a mountain cell is N, then that mountain is part of a vertical straight section of length N. The sums of the digits above and below the mountain within that section must differ by N. Each flat road cell lies on the path. The path must travel straight horizontally through each flat road cell. If the digit in a flat road cell is N, then that road is part of a horizontal straight section of length N. The sums of the digits to the left and right of the road within that section must differ by N. Each chequered flag lies on the path. The path must turn at each flag, with one straight horizontal stage and one straight vertical stage meeting at the flag. If the digit in a flag cell is N, then both stages have length N, including the flag cell itself. The sums of the non-flag digits in the two stages must differ by N.
Soigneur (standing man) cells are not on the path. A digit in a Soigneur cell indicates the number of path cells in the (up to) 8 surrounding cells.

title: The Music In The Fog: WHAT A Sudoku Puzzle!
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The Pi Guy has been following the channel for a while (thank you) and has made a really fantastic fog-of-war sudoku with one of the most innovative break-ins we've seen. Lots going on musically today too :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/jcj5nibbdm

Rules:
Sudoku: Normal sudoku rules apply; put the digits 1 to 9 once each into every row, column & 3 by 3 box.
(U2 - One, Fleetwood Mac - Everywhere)

Fog: The grid is covered in fog, some of which has been cleared. Place digits correctly to clear more fog. Fog may clear at any time and from anywhere in the grid. 
(Madness - Grey Day, Lighthouse Family - Lifted, KT Tunstall - Suddenly I See)

Cages: The digits in each cage (area with a dotted outline) must sum to the same total, which is to be deduced.
(Coldplay - In My Place, Keane - Somewhere [Sum Where] Only We Know)

Thermometers: Digits on a thermometer must increase from the bulb (the end with the circle) to the tip.
(M People - Moving On Up)

Renbans: Digits on a purple line (hollow) must form a consecutive sequence in some order, with no repeats (e.g. 1-2-3).
(Snow Patrol - Run)

Nabners: Digits on a yellow line (normal) must not be consecutive (e.g. 1-4-9, no digit is consecutive with any of the others).
(Coldplay - Yellow, Keane - We Might As Well Be Strangers)

Dutch whispers: Digits in cells that are next to each other on an orange line (dashed) must be at least 4 apart (e.g. 1-9-5).
(Imagine Dragons - Amsterdam, Coldplay - A Whisper, Dire Straits - So Far Away)

[All lines go through at least two cells and they never branch or cut off. Lines and thermometers may move diagonally.]

No repeats on a constraint: When considered together, all clues that follow the same constraint (e.g. renbans) must include each of the digits 1 to 9 exactly once (the renbans could be 1-2-3, 4-5 & 6-7-8-9).
(Keane - Everybody’s Changing, Bryan Adams - The Only One)

title: God-Tier Fog Sudoku Makes My Brain Hurt!
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We must have missed this fog sudoku from Kaktuslav when it was first released.... it's called Reciprocals and Mark suggested Simon have a go at it today. When Simon read the rules, he wondered if Mark was having a joke at his expense!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/gf8l5f4s64

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin–Yang: shade some cells in the grid so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2×2 region is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. Every shaded cell containing digit x has value 1/x; every unshaded cell has value equal to its digit. Product/Sum cages: each cage has a corner mark in the leftmost cell of its top row identifying its type. If it shows Σ=X, the values in the cage sum to X; if it shows Π=X, the values in the cage multiply to X (X is not necessarily an integer). Digits or values MAY repeat within a cage. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals their own cell and may also lift fog elsewhere in the grid. No guessing is required.

title: You're A Better Man Than I Am, Sudoku Genius (aka Kaktuslav!).
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What an incredible discovery greets us in tonight's video. It's called Coldulo, it's by Kaktuslav and, when you read the rules, you will wonder (rightly) how this can possibly solve... To paraphrase Kipling, you're a better man than I am, Kaktuslav!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/8spurrnmcc

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The nine marked cells contain the digits 1–9, each exactly once. If a marked cell contains the digit N, then every vertical group of N consecutive cells in its column has remainders 0, 1, ..., N−1, in some order, when its digits are divided by N. Such a group may start anywhere in the column; it does not need to contain the marked cell. For example, if a marked cell contains 4, then every four consecutive cells in its column have remainders 0, 1, 2, 3 modulo 4, in some order.

title: The Most Requested Puzzle Of Recent Times!
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've had so many requests to attempt tonight's puzzle: Lupin's Loop 4 - Surrounded by Rab3ron. We've done the first three on the channel but such was the reputation of this one Simon wanted to wait for a day when he had a relatively long window to record! This is a seriously cool and interesting sudoku - can you see how it works?

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/0do1zxouyi

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. A greater-than symbol points towards the smaller number. Draw two metro lines that travel orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, either with themselves or with each other, which eventually close to form two loops. Thick black walls cannot be crossed by the lines. One loop must lie entirely inside the other, so the outer loop completely surrounds the inner loop. Every station must lie on a loop. All cells on the same loop share the same parity (the two loops may have the same or different parities). A digit in a red sensor equals the number of cells visited by either loop in the 3×3 box centred on that cell. A digit in a station equals the total number of stations containing that digit. The mirror cell has mirrored parity, meaning its parity is considered to be the opposite of its real parity. If a loop passes through it, treat the cell according to this mirrored parity.

title: The One And Only Fog Sudoku!
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
When a sudoku is recommended to us by Marty Sears we listen because Marty knows a thing or two about puzzles. Tonight's sudoku is a debut by PrissyP - real name Olli - made for his girlfriend, Lina's, birthday tomorrow. It would be ungallant to reveal her age but we can tell you this is a stunning present!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/kj2qd0ug0d

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Most of the grid is hidden. Cells are revealed as they are correctly solved, gradually uncovering the puzzle and its constraints. No guessing is necessary. Pink lines are Renban lines: The digits on each pink line form a set of consecutive numbers, in any order. 
The digits on ALL Renban lines, taken together, sum to X. Yellow lines are Addition lines: The digits on each yellow line sum to X. Red lines are Multiplication lines: The digits on each red line have a product of X. Little Killer clues: The digits on each indicated arrowed diagonal sum to X. 
A digit may be used in at most one type of constraint. Eg if a 2 appears on a Renban line, then no 2 may appear on any Addition line, Multiplication line, or Little Killer diagonal. The value of X is not given and must be deduced by the solver.

title: This Puzzle Is EXTRAORDINARY.
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Hard to know where to begin when describing tonight's sudoku. It's called Stishovite and it is like it's been hewn out of nature. The imagination and sheer mental firepower that's gone in to its creation is pretty incredible: bellsita and Wisteria Fall (with assistance from XeonRisq) have made a (very) hard but extraordinary puzzle.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/1tzwquyhbb

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
No digit may appear more than once on a particular clue type. 
Clue types: 
1) Adjacent digits on a green line differ by 5 or more; 
2) Purple lines must contain a set of consecutive non-repeating digits in any order; 
3) Any sequence of 3 adjacent digits along a teal line must contain a complete set of residuals modulo 3, i.e: one from (1,4,7), one from (2,5,8) and one from (3,6,9); 
4) Digits along a red line must alternate between odd and even; 
5) Digits may not repeat within a cage; 
6) The grey circle contain an odd digit. The grey squares contain even digits. 
7) Cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); 
8) Cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive.

title: This Sudoku Is "Kind Of Insane"!!
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Just looking at the grid, it could only be a Marty Sears puzzle! It's called Clone Count and it's one of the most original sudokus we've seen in a while. It has some (very) unusual ideas under its bonnet and is an absolute blast to spend time with!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ib9r4zuejw

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit 1-9 is depicted in this puzzle by a strange symbol. Deduce which symbol stands for which digit, and keep track using the key on the right.This grid contains numerous blob-like alien creatures, each consisting of two horizontally adjacent cells. Some blobs are shown; the others are invisible and must be located. Blobs do not overlap each other. Some blobs are clones of each other, ie: they contain the exact same two digits in the same order. A blob's left-hand digit always indicates exactly how many instances of that blob (including itself) exist in the grid. If there is a circular label in the centre of a blob, its symbol indicates the sum of the blob's two cells.

title: Unlocking Sudoku's Secret Code
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for Vythic and their puzzle, Splatter Code. This is an approachable chaos construction (such things do exist!) and has some lovely logic involving a new type of sudoku line.
Also, if you're a patron, do check out Simon's new 2hr video solve of GCHQ's Puzzle Of The Year!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/0ugsgegaxv

Rules:
Digits are not repeated in rows, columns, or regions. 
The board is divided into nine hidden regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally-connected cells. Fill every region, row and column with the digitis 1 to 9, once each. 
A digit on an arrow indicates the length of the uninterrupted run of cells immediately beyond the arrow, in the arrow's direction, that belong to the same region as the arrow cell. Summit Lines: Digits along a blue line must be ascending or descending, with 1 and 9 reversing the ascension/descension. (eg if digits along a blue line are 2-5-6-9-8-5, the sequence is ascending until the 9 causes a descension). Cells separated by an X sum to 10, and cells separated by a V sum to 5.

title: Can You Count The Dominoes?!
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It sounds so straightforward doesn't it... Count Some Dominoes... well, it still requires more thought than you might think in this beautiful sudoku from mellowrobinson. It's packed with original logic and solves likes a dream - the only debate is over the difficulty... see what you think!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/27qnv0oduh

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine non-overlapping regions each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Fill every cell with a digit from 1-9 so there aren't repeats in any row, column, or region. A domino is two cells that share an edge. The digit in a caged cell indicates how many dominoes entirely within its region sum to the indicated total. Dominoes that are only half in the region don't count. Dominoes may overlap. Digits separated by an X sum to 10, and digits separated by a V sum to 5.

title: A Positive Outlook for Negative Constraints
description:
Here's where you can try Quadrants by Daniel Hanson: https://sudokupad.app/1b7rrbig2u 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is divided into four quadrants. Each quadrant obeys a constraint, and no constraint extends outside of its quadrant. In the NW quadrant (boxes 1, 2, 4, 5), cells separated by a single knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. In the NE quadrant (boxes 2, 3, 5, 6), where two cells are separated by a black dot, the digit in one cell is double the digit in the other; all possible black dots for that quadrant are given. In the SW quadrant (boxes 4, 5, 7, 8), where two cells are separated by a white dot, the digit in one cell is consecutive with the digit in the other; all possible white dots for that quadrant are given. In the SE quadrant (boxes 5, 6, 8, 9), digits separated by a V sum to 5 and digits separated by an X sum to ten; all possible V's and X's for that quadrant are given.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. On a black dot, one digits is double the other. On a white dot, digits are consecutive. Digits separated by V sum to 5. ALL such dominoes are given. Digits separated by X sum to 10. NOT ALL such dominoes are given. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5 – on a 2-cell green line, their difference is exactly 5. Digits on a purple line form a consecutive, non-repeating set in any order. Digits on a marked diagonal do not repeat.

title: Football or Sudoku? Easy Decision!
description:
Here's where you can try Red Dead Difference by Mateo99: https://sudokupad.app/30nule6bb2 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each red line has a value, V, determined by the formula: V = L - B where: L is the sum of the digits on the line; B is the total sum of all digits that are not on the line, but lie within any 3x3 box that the line enters. For example, if a line visits both Box 1 and Box 2, B is the sum of all digits in Box 1 and Box 2 that are not part of the line. 
The values, V, of all lines in the grid must form a set of consecutive, non-repeating positive integers. Additionally, all red lines act as slow thermometers. Digits must never decrease moving along the line starting from the bulb (i.e., each digit must be equal to or greater than the previous digit). The bulb end of each line is not marked and must be determined by the solver. On a white dot, cells contain consecutive digits. On a black dot, one digit is double the other.

description:

Happy birthday Oddlyeven! Tonight we try one of his puzzles that's intended to most closely resemble his own style!! It's called Kelowna and it's just very, very clever. It's like a series of miniature brainteasers, chained together and packaged into sudoku form :)

title: Explore a New Maze!
description:
Here's where you can try Whispers in the Maze by Ryan Adams: https://sudokupad.app/zyutsxhylp 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Starting in the middle of the grid at row 5 column 5, draw a path through the maze to the exit at row 3 column 1 where the valid path forms a continuous German Whisper line - adjacent digits on the line have a difference of at least 5. The path must be orthogonally connected (no diagonal moves) and cannot pass through any of the thick black walls.
Digits separated by a white Kropki dot have a difference of 1. If an arrow separates two digits, it points to the smaller digit. The two digits on the diamonds are the same. 
The fog in the top corner of the grid will be cleared when all instances of a digit (to be deduced) have been placed.

title: Getting Even in an Odd Way
description:
Here's where you can attempt Oddly Enough Even Dots Help by DC: https://sudokupad.app/hignojf8ll 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a grey square is even. A digit in a grey circle is odd. There is a maximum of 2 consecutive even or odd cells in any horizontal or vertical direction.
Digits in cells joined by a green dot are the same parity (both odd or both even).  Digits in cells joined by a red dot are the opposite parity (one odd, one even). Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive. On a black dot, one digit is double the other.
A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal using only cells of the same parity as the first cell, eg. if R1C2 is odd, the sum of all odd cells on that diagonal is 16.

title: Our Longest Ever Video...!! Rat Run 40: The Big One (S3:E20)
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

And you can hear Simon recite the story so far here:
https://youtu.be/kCF9uLrsEus

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Where do we start? Some years ago, Marty Sears released a sudoku puzzle about the adventures of a little rat, Finkz, and a story commenced. Tonight, with the 40th puzzle in the series, that story reaches its epic conclusion in the most extraordinary way. Marty has done it (yet) again: a puzzle of staggering complexity, wit, size (!) and imagination in we, once more, are tasked with finding a way for our rat to reach the cupcake. 
Oh and can we mention that this is the longest single video we've ever released on Cracking The Cryptic?! Simon was NEVER going to give up on this one!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/nfqumwpslw

Rules:
Finkz must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Fill the grid with the digits 0-9. Divide the maze floor into pentomino shaped regions (groups of five orthogonally connected cells.) Every cell belongs to exactly one pentomino region. Every thick maze wall sits between two separate regions. All five cells of a region must be filled with the same digit. Regions that touch along an edge (even through a wall) may not contain the same digit, and must not be the same shaped pentomino (rotations and reflections count as the same shape.) Most of the maze is obscured with fog. Correctly filling a pentomino will clear some fog somewhere. No guessing is necessary. A purple probe is a diamond shaped device built into a wall between two neighbouring pentomino regions. The digit on the attached circle indicates the total number of cells visited within those two neighbouring regions. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. If a goldenberry sits between two digits, they are not consecutive (or the same.) A purple arrow sits between two different digits and points towards the smaller digit. Finkz may only pass through a purple arrow in the direction it's pointing. If a floor panel is illuminated with a blue square, it lies on Finkz' path and indicates that a spike in brain activity was detected in response to that digit. Two cells visited adjacently along the path may never sum to a prime number. (Note: 0 and 1 are not prime.)

title: Does So-called "Sudoku Expert" Make A  Mistake??
description:
NOTE: Simon has recorded his solve of Marty Sears' Rat Run 40: The Big One. This will be released on the channel tomorrow night because the video is so long it will take most of this evening to upload it on to YouTube. Shoutout to whoever guesses the length of the video closest in tonight's comments!! 

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've had this Fog-Of-War sudoku, Bullseye! by Lorena, recommended to us a lot over the last month or two. It features one of the great preambles and, without wanting to give too much away, it's well worth having a go at (and it is very approachable!)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/rrhrws2x7f

Rules:
Oh, no! The Wicked Witch Lorena has cursed you with forgetting all numbers! Fortunately for you, the International Accord on Curses, Hexes and Jinxes of 1692 forbids unbreakable curses so, like it or not, she must ensure that there is a way to get out of it. It’s the law! But that doesn’t mean she has to make it easy. Cruel as she is, she has determined that the only way for you to fully break the curse will be to solve this sudoku. Luckily, as the fog lifts in your mind, the numbers will gradually start to come back to you.
Once a given digit appears in the grid for the first time, you may use it to fill in cells. If a digit hasn’t yet made an appearance, you are not allowed to use it (pencilmarks are okay). Placing a correct digit may or may not remove fog anywhere in the grid.  Digits cannot repeat in any row, column or marked 3x3 box.  Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a 2:1 ratio (i.e. one of the digits must be double the other).  Grey palindrome lines must read the same in both directions. Adjacent digits in a green German whispers line must differ by at least 5.
Breaking these rules or trying to guess digits at random to clear the fog might end up with you being turned into a frog, so consider yourself warned.
Note: Yes, you remember the concept of numbers, so you can understand the rules. You’re still not allowed to use them until you see them in the grid. Nice try, though.

title: Colouring Grids is FUN!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Xin Yang v2 by PuzzleTank: https://sudokupad.app/qc37ejydvj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Digits along an arrow must sum to the two-digit total given in the arrow's attached pill (read from left to right).
Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area can be either entirely shaded or unshaded. Each arrow total is a two digit number to be read as (X,Y). The X value (tens digit) indicates how many SHADED cells can be seen from that cell in ONLY the HORIZONTAL direction including itself. The Y value (ones digit) indicates how many UNSHADED cells can be seen from the cell in ONLY the VETRICAL direction including itself. (The other shading blocks vision). Cells separated by a Kropki Dot MUST be of opposite shading.

title: An Electric Birthday For This Sudoku Solver
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's Simon's birthday - (25 in case you're wondering!) - so he's giving himself a present by having a go at the new Lupin's Loop sudoku from Rab3aron! This is number 3 in the series and, again, it's superb with original and interesting logic.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/zsmtekox43

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a single electricity cable that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, which eventually closes into a loop. The loop must pass through every hut. Water drops mark river borders that the loop cannot cross. Any two cells that are adjacent along the loop must contain non-consecutive digits, unless the loop is passing through a white dot (where consecutive digits may appear). Any two huts directly connected by the loop form a segment (including both huts). A digit in a hut equals the length of the longest segment containing it.

title: Only Solved 10 Times Ever... Can He Make It 11?
description:
We are so close to 700,000 Subscribers... If you aren't subscribed, please do consider it :)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An incredibly interesting and unusual fog-of-war sudoku tonight from Pulsar and FischmitFahrrad called The Neighbours Are Whispering. We're not sure how the idea for this one emerged but it's been incredibly well constructed... it's not terribly easy to finish though!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/euq3xbt4hm

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Doublers: If a digit within a box is equal to its relative position in that box (read from left to right and top to bottom), the value of that digit is doubled for the Whispering Neighbours constraint. Each digit from 1-9 is doubled exactly once, and each row and column must contain exactly one doubler. Boxes may contain zero, one, or more than one doubler. Whispering Neighbours: Each cell in the grid has at least one orthogonally adjacent cell such that their values differ by at least 5. Gated Communities: Orthogonally adjacent cells that are separated by cage borders have values that differ by less than 5. Digits and values may repeat inside a cage. Cages cannot be divided into smaller cages. The grid is covered in fog, which will clear completely after certain digits are placed correctly.

title: Complete Madness with Pentominoes
description:
Here's where you can try Pent Up by Daniel Buckeldee: https://sudokupad.app/f0t3wo1l0n 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Tile the 9x9 grid except R5C5 with pentominoes (two are given). Every cell should appear in exactly one pentomino. Each pentomino shape should be unique (rotations are not allowed, reflections are allowed). Within a pentomino, for every horizontal domino the righthand cell is larger than the left, and for every vertical domino the lower cell is larger than the upper cell (e.g. R2C4 is less than R3C4 and R3C2 is less than R3C3). Digits may repeat in a pentomino.

title: How to End the Dream Sequence
description:
Here's where you can try 1 Hotel and a Dream by Cassinii: https://sudokupad.app/jqg2me00dc 
Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. A clue outside the grid gives the digit that must be placed in the Nth position in that row or column, where N is the digit in the cell next to the clue.

And here's 1 Last Dream by Cassinii: https://sudokupad.app/dq0yiosab8 
Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. The grey regions contain the same set of digits in the same arrangement. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 3. Digits on a magenta line form a non-repeating, consecutive set in any order. Digits on a grey thermometer strictly increase from bulb to tip. Digits in a cage do not repeat, and sum to the small number in the top left of the cage. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits either side of a white dot are consecutive. On a black dot one digit is double the other.

title: A Sudoku With Only 1 Given Digit?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This sort of title heralds a sudoku by Aad van de Wetering, the Dutch wizard. This one is called 24 Squares! and it's "classic Aad" - a simple ruleset and a surprisingly deep and satisfying logical exercise. This puzzle does not play to any sudoku strengths Simon may have...!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/oso53h7rd2

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line contains a square number reading from left to right (or in the case of the line in r3c1, from top to bottom). eg If r8c7 was a 2 then r7c8 must be a 5 (to give the square number 25). (As an aide memoire, all 2-digit squares and 3-digit squares (without zeroes or a repeated digit) are: 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 169, 196, 256, 289, 324, 361, 529, 576, 625, 729, 784, 841, 961).

title: Is This the New Most Important Total?
description:
Here's where you can try The One and Only Sum by Lithium-Ion: https://sudokupad.app/jl4sby2gl2 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits that are in a 1:2 ratio. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Neighboring digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Neighboring digits along an orange line must differ by at least 4. A pink line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. Along a gray thermometer, digits must strictly increase from the bulb end. Each set of three consecutive cells along a peach entropic line must contain one low (123), one medium (456) and one high (789) digit. Box borders divide the blue region sum line into segments with the same sum. The sum of all digits that belong to one constraint type (e.g. all digits on black dots) is the same for each of the eight constraint types in this puzzle and must be deduced by the solver.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We go back into the annals of time tonight to try an older puzzle by Michael Lefkowitz (Juggler) called Mind The Gap. This is a 5/5 difficulty sudoku with a beautiful central idea - if you find it, you'll probably solve it quickly!!  Good luck :)

https://sudokupad.app/tl8tkze8mn

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a yellow safety strip are in a 2:1 ratio (ie one is double the other.) Extend the 'gap' (ie the grey lines) along cell edges so that it forms a single loop, which cannot touch itself. Even and odd digits may not touch except across the gap. Draw a path from cell centre to cell centre from the blue dot to the red pin, which may move orthogonally or diagonally. It can't cross or touch the gap, except at yellow safety strips. Adjacent digits on the path differ by at least 3.

title: Beautiful, Beautiful Sudoku
description:
Here's where you can attempt Eye of the Beholder by Oskode & Calvinball: https://sudokupad.app/65spa2e9w3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each question mark acts as a stand-in for a digit, which must be deduced for each question mark. Each circle contains 2 digits. The 2 digits must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle (if a digit repeats in a circle, it must appear twice). Digits along an arrow sum to a two-digit number. This number is a concatenation of BOTH digits in the attached circle.
For clarity: A circle with the digits {1, 9} would be surrounded by at least one copy each of the digits 1 and 9 and could have arrows that summed to either 19 or 91. Its arrows could not sum to 11 nor 99, this would require a {1, 1} circle surrounded by two 1s or a {9, 9} circle surrounded by two 9s respectively.)

title: Help NASA! Solve This Puzzle.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Apologies for the late arrival of this video... our first attempt to upload it caused a "video processing" failure, which we haven't seen before.
We hope it's worth the wait however for this fantastic sequel for Rab3aron's Lupin's Loop series. This one is called Space Invasion and it's just wonderful (hence its 99% rating on Logic Masters). Enjoy.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/l00604nlbr

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a single route that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, which eventually closes into a loop. The loop must pass through every planet. Thick black borders represent black holes that the route cannot cross. A digit in a satellite dish equals the number of loop cells in the 3×3 box centred on that cell. Along the loop, one parity forces the route to turn (making a 90° angle) while the other forces it to continue straight (making a 180° angle), it is up to the solver to determine which parity corresponds to which behaviour. Any two cells that are adjacent along the loop must contain non-consecutive digits unless the loop is passing through a white dot (where consecutive digits may appear).

This evening's musical outro was The Blower's Daughter by Damien Rice but we got Copyrighted for it (so at least it must have been recognisable!). In the unlikely event there's an overwhelming response from people wanting to hear it we'll upload it on Patreon as a bonus but, frankly, you'll probably be quite relieved you didn't hear it X)

title: The Return Of Choco Banana!! Fog Sudoku At Its Finest
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy birthday SamuPiano whose puzzle Foggy Banana Split is the one Simon tackles tonight. This is a fantastic use of the Choco Banana logic puzzle, which first appeared in a Nikoli magazine a few years ago. Challenging and SO satisfying from start to finish.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/23phi9d5m7

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from the surrounding area. Shade all cells either brown (chocolate) or yellow (banana) such that all chocolate areas are rectangular, and no banana areas are rectangular. All lines move orthogonally and end in circles on either end. Lines do not cross, branch, or share cells. Circles may be contained in either chocolate or banana cells. Circles indicate the size of the area in which they are contained. The digit in a circled cell with a line attached also gives the number of cells of the same shading as the circled cell along the line, including the endpoints. Digits along a line must sum to a two-digit number, where the 'tens' digit is in one circle and the 'ones' digit is in the other. Cells separated by an X sum to 10. Cells separated by a V sum to 5.

title: A Foggy Secret Revealed... Rat Run 39: Together Apart (S3:E19)
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

And you can hear Simon recite the story so far here:
https://youtu.be/kCF9uLrsEus

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What a week - a second Rat Run puzzle and we're reaching the end of this epic tale from the extraordinary mind of Marty Sears. This episode is called Together Apart and, if you manage to finish it, the reward is some revelations about what has actually been happening to the rats over the course 1974 and 1975! 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/pja7uaxak9

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Much of the grid is obscured by fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. If a starfruit sits between two digits, they always have the same sum, to be determined. Every coloured circular button must be visited. The digit on a button indicates the number of cells that the rat moves after the button to arrive in a different 3x3 box. (Eg: if the rat moves immediately from the button into a new 3x3 box, the button would contain a 1.) A digit on a path may not be consecutive with the digit visited immediately before it.

title: The Amazing Sudoku Map
description:
Here's where you can try North Side & South Side by Haleypro: https://sudokupad.app/3xdi7kf6ab  and https://sudokupad.app/d05ho9qchh  
Normal sudoku rules apply. The two puzzles must be solved in tandem. The puzzles overlap at the Loop in R9C9 (so eg. R9C7 in North Side and R1C6 in South Side contain the same digit). All cells with an airplane contain the same digit across both puzzles.
Red Line: Parity line (cells alternate in parity). Purple Line: Zipper line (digits an equal distance from the center sum to the digit in the center). Yellow Line: Nabner line (no two digits can be consecutive or identical). Blue Line: Region Sum line (box borders divide the line into segments with an equal sum). Green Line: German Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 5 or more). Orange Line: Dutch Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 4 or more). Brown Line: Slow thermo (moving from the bulb, each digit is the same or higher). Pink Line: Renban line (a set of consecutive digits in any order).

title: How Does He Keep Doing This?! Rat Run 38: Synchonicity (S3:E18)
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

And you can hear Simon recite the story so far here:
https://youtu.be/kCF9uLrsEus

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon returns from Carne (County Mayo) not wanting to see another Guinness to find the latest Rat Run sudoku waiting for him. This one, number 38, is called Synchronicity and it's one of Marty Sears' best ever... which is saying quite something. The idea behind this is completely ridiculous and the execution... well, it's pretty astonishing if you stop to think about it.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/up5nrki10o

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. There is no space to move diagonally in this maze. If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant, one is double the other. A purple arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between, and may only be passed through in the direction it's pointing. In this experiment, any two digits visited adjacently along a path must be different parities (one is odd and the other is even), and also have a difference of at least 5.

description:

Here's where you can try Oops! Bumped the Table by PhyDraLey: https://sudokupad.app/vnd2slg4jx 
Normal sudoku rules apply. I accidentally hit the table, moving all my carefully placed dots around. All kropki dots have been moved by half a cell (meaning each dot on a cell must come from one of that cells edges.) No two dots were in the same location before moving. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive. On a black dot one digit is double the other.

title: A Sudoku Recommended By One Of The All-Time Greats
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight we have a debut on the channel for Sven-Ole Behrend and his sudoku, Disorienting Hits. This has been recommended to us by none other than Marty Sears (who knows a thing or two about this ruleset too, given he invented it!) And, as we should expect, this is rather wonderful. Not too difficult but with some absolutely lovely logic to discover.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/31wnj4k03o

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one is double the other. Beige Lines are hitlines: Digits along a hitline do not repeat. One end of a hitline (to be determined by the solver) is the starting point. The digit N in the starting point indicates that exactly N digits along that hitline match their position along the hitline, counting from the starting point. Eg: A valid hitline of length 6 could be given by: 4 - 2 - 3 - 9 - 5 - 6, where 4 is the starting point of the hitline (as the 2,3,5 and 6 are in the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 6th position respectively).

title: A Candidate For "Puzzle Of The Year".
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This puzzle, Vicissitudes by Nicolas Duhail, has been touted to us as a contender for Puzzle Of The Year. And now we've had a go at it, we agree. This is ridiculously brilliant. An absurd concept that somehow meshes together impeccably. Incredible.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/b3wa450x40

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be completely shaded or unshaded. The shading splits the line into segments with equal sums. Digits may not repeat within a segment.

title: The Thermometers Under The Sudoku Fog!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A class fog-of-war sudoku tonight from FIT7Y called Measuring The Fog. It features a small twist on the thermometer ruleset and this leads to some brilliantly inventive logic throughout. 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/1959ln4ivg

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Correctly placed digits will clear fog from the surrounding cells. No guessing is required. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb to the tip. Thermometers move orthogonally through the grid, and do not branch, overlap, or intersect. One of the digits on every thermometer must be the length of that thermometer.

description:
Here's where you can try 4 Magic by BlackRaven: https://sudokupad.app/v38zh5blzk 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw an orthogonally conected path that does not branch or touch itself, not even diagonally. The path starts at one square, ends at the other and visits each box at least once. Any set of 4 consecutive cells on the path contains four digits with different modularity when divided by 4 (one digit from each of these sets: {1,5,9}, {2,6}, {3,7}, {4,8}). Arrow cells are off the path and count the number of path cells in the indicated direction. Circle cells are off the path and count the number of path cells in the 8 cells around it. Digits on a purple line form a non-repeating consecutive sequence in any order. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with an equal sum. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.

title: Sudoku Expert Gets Played Like A Fool!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears has had a lot of practice when it comes to playing Simon for a fool but, annoyingly, he gets to do it again today!! This sudoku (Once A Copycat, Always A Copycat) was made as a birthday present for the inventor of "Copycat cells", Scojo,  and Marty demonstrates an innate understanding of how these cells work... Will you get fooled too?!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/kn2gf9mjm7

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Nine copycat cells exist in the grid. They all contain the same digit (to be deduced), but they all have a different value. You can use the circles at the bottom to keep track. The value of a copycat cell equals the digit in the cell that is 180° rotationally opposite itself. Eg: If r1c3 is a copycat cell, then its value equals the digit in r9c7. For two adjacent values along a grey line, one can always be divided by the other to give an exact integer - ie; one is a multiple of the other. If a black dot sits between two cells, the value of one is double the value of the other. If a yellow dot sits between two cells, their values are not consecutive or the same.

title: Professor Lupin's First Sudoku Loop
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An exciting new series begins from Rab3aron themed around loops (we think) starting with Lupin's Loop 1... this is a magnificent puzzle too - so good that we're eagerly awaiting the second sudoku - could this be the new Rat Run?!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/3p3nivu3o6

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single road that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, and which eventually closes into a loop. The road must pass through every house. Borders marked with traffic lights are controlled intersections that the road cannot cross. The bold 3×3 borders divide the road into segments. Within each segment, all digits must be pairwise prime (that is, any two digits in the same segment share no common factor greater than 1). A digit in a house equals the length of the segment containing it, while a digit in a speed camera counts how many road cells appear in the ENTIRE row of that camera, including the camera cell itself. Note: A segment does not necessarily contain a house. Any segment of length 1 must contain the digit 1.

title: 10 x 10 Sudoku? More Cells to go Wrong in ...
description:
Here's where you can try Whispering Fives by M.K.: https://sudokupad.app/wdb9oj31j6 
Every row, column and 2x5 box contains the digits 0 to 9 once each. Digits in a cage sum to the small number in its corner (if given). Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Each cage starts one straight green line from its left cell going either up, left, or down. The two digits in a cage represent the sum of the digits on the line originating from that cage. For example, if a cage contains 1 and 9, the digits on its line sum to 19. 0 is a valid starting digit. A line cannot enter another cage, but may cross or overlap another line.

title: These Sudoku Rats Are Incredible!! Rat Run 37: Fruitful (S3:E17)
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

And you can hear Simon recite the story so far here:
https://youtu.be/kCF9uLrsEus

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another astonishing "sudoku" in the most extraordinary sudoku series of all time. Marty Sears's Rat Run No. 37 "Fruitful" will leave you scratching you head in despair and admiration in equal measure as you try and find he logical paths for our intrepid rats. We reckon this is one of the easiest puzzles to make a logical error in that we've ever seen... let's hope Simon didn't!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9qx3iprv0x

Rules:
Fill the grid with the digits 1-9, so that in each row and column, one of the digits 1-9 is missing, and one of the digits is repeated. Every digit from 1-9 is missing from exactly one row and one column, and repeated in exactly one row and one column. Use the orange arrows to keep track of missing digits, and the blue arrows to keep track of repeated digits. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. A red X may not be passed through, and sits between two digits that sum to 10. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. If a goldenberry sits between two digits, they are not consecutive (or the same.) In this experiment, a rat's path is divided into segments by any fruit she eats. The digits on each segment have the same sum, to be determined. This 'segment sum' may be different for Finkz and Phinx.

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Some cells are covered with fog. Filling in correct digits may lift fog somewhere in the puzzle. The digit on a White chess piece counts how many of the squares that the piece can legally move to contain a digit different from itself. The digit on a Black chess piece counts how many of the squares that the piece can legally move to contain the same digit as itself, not counting itself. Each player has exactly 1 king and at most 8 pawns, 2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops and 1 queen. Legal moves exactly follow the normal rules of chess): Pieces can capture, pieces block movement, and moves that leave your king in check are not legal. White pawns start on row 8 and black pawns start on row 2, counting from the top. Castling, promotion and en-passant are not relevant in this puzzle.

title: Some Assembly Required - Very Few Have Achieved It!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Assembly Required by Staxis: https://sudokupad.app/vanmy8509l 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Arrows, region sum lines, Renban lines, Dutch whisper lines, and parity lines are not given and must be placed. A white circle must be on an arrow (circle or line), a blue circle on a region sum line, a pink circle on a Renban line, an orange circle on a Dutch whisper, and a red circle on a parity line. An arrow circle must have one or more attached lines. A region sum line must visit multiple regions. A Renban lines, Dutch whisper line, or parity line must be at least 2 cells long.
Digits on each line sum of an arrow to the digit in the attached circled cell. Box borders divide a region sum lines into segments with an equal sum. A renban line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Adjacent digits along a Dutch whisper line have a difference of at least 4. Adjacent digits along a parity line have different parity.
There are exactly 9 cells on arrows (circles and lines combined) and they contain all numbers 1-9. The same is true for region sums, Renbans, Dutch whispers, and parity lines. No cell is a member of more than one of these extra regions, though lines may cross diagonally.
