title: Total Sudoku Genius In A 6x6 Grid
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A few weeks ago, ThePedallingPianist celebrated his birthday and Marty Sears made him a present in the form of this sudoku. It's a 6x6 puzzle with unusual rules but the way this unfolds is a close to magic as you'll find in this hobby. Completely, ridiculously, brilliant.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/bpxci0jt2o

Rules:
Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that digits don't repeat in any row, column or box. Each row contains a 6-digit number reading forwards and another reading backwards. Each column contains a 6-digit number reading downwards, and another reading upwards. These 24 numbers are ranked from 1-24, from lowest to highest. There are no tied ranks, so none of the numbers are the same. A purple circle contains the rank of the 6-digit number it points at (reading in the direction the arrow is pointing.) If two digits are joined by a black dot, one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a red dot, one is odd and the other is even. If two digits are joined by a yellow dot, they are NOT consecutive.

title: Which Rat Is Best At Sudoku?! Rat Run: One Year Earlier
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

And you can hear Simon recite the story so far here:
https://youtu.be/kCF9uLrsEus

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Thank goodness there is a Rat Run sudoku today... Simon was worried last week when he saw the next in the series was scheduled for 13 May but it turns out all is well in the world as here's an episode based on how Finkz actually got selected for her task in the first place. Marty's genius shines through as always and now we can't wait for next week!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ceyzcgb9os

Rules:
For the final preliminary 'free-roam' trial, the nine shortlisted rats were placed in a 9x9 space, and their movements were observed and recorded. Each of the digits 1-9 appeared in each row and column. 
OBSERVATIONS: 
Every cell in the grid was visited, exactly once; 
No rat's path contained any repeated digits; 
No rat chose to move diagonally at any point; 
Every 2x2 area was visited by at least 2 rats; 
No two rats started on the same digit; 
No two rats ended on the same digit; 
All blackcurrants and redcurrants were eaten; and
No grapes were eaten. 

If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5.

title: THIS IS SUDOKU SPARTA!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Nicolas Duhail is a quite brilliant constructor - he almost has no right to be brilliant so often - publishing so many sudokus that the recommmendations we get can hardly keep up! Tonight we attempt This Is Sparta! It's themed on the 300 Spartans who resisted Xerxes and the Persians at the battle of Thermopylae. Can you save the sudoku kingdom?!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/oiqfym9ehw

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The product of the digits along a hollow orange line is equal to 300. Every set of three sequential digits along a teal modular line contains digits with three different remainders when divided by 3. title: Puzzle Expert Attempts Something Stupid...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
More Marty Sears magic tonight with the most inappropriately titled puzzle to date... it maybe called Something Stupid but there is absolutely nothing stupid about this one. It is highly original and completely captivating.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/4wlunbtlaq

Rules:
Every gold circle contains a different digit. In any row or column, its circle indicates the number of distinct digits that appears in that row or column. Any of these digits can be repeated any number of times in order to fill the row / column. Eg: one particular row has a circle containing a 3, meaning that row only contains three distinct digits - a valid example would be 173777131. Entering a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. Along a lavender line, digits that are the same distance from the central spot sum to the digit on that central spot. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. If a red dot sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a black dot sits between two digits, one is double the other.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's ChinStrap's birthday so we're celebrating with one of his puzzles: Up Up and Away, a fascinating 6x6 featuring a long purple thermometer!! The ruleset is unusual and resultant sudoku is interesting and clever (without being too monstrous)... it's almost like ChinStrap gave us a present on his birthday!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/sr3ev8r4sd

Rules:
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits on the slow thermo may not decrease starting at the bulb. Outside clues on the slow thermo must contain a digit, and that digit indicates the length of the first ascending sequence in that direction. For example, a row with 142536 gives a left clue of 2 (1, 4) and a right clue of 1 (6). ie a sequence can be only one cell.

title: Ouch My Poor Poor Brain: Sudoku At Its Maddest!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What a ruleset... It's not that it's difficult to understand but it's quite hard to know what on Earth to do with it!! Oddlyeven decides he will break our collective brains with this one. It's called Yin Yang Doubler Uniqueness but it could simply be called 'AAAAGGGHHHH'!!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yl0n45rfll

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Yin Yang Doublers: Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthoganally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 may be all shaded or all unshaded. A shaded cell has a value equal to twice its digit. An unshaded cell has a value equal to twice its digit minus one (double the digit first, then subtract one).
Uniqueness: On each of the constraints below, values do not repeat anywhere in the puzzle. For example, if there is a shaded 5 (value 10) on a renban, shaded 5 can't appear anywhere else on a renban, but unshaded 5 could because it has a value of 9.
Renban: Values on a purple line form a set of consecutive numbers with no repeats.
Arrows: Values along an arrow sum the value in that arrow's circle.
X: Two cells joined by an X have values that sum to 10.
Black Dots: Two cells joined by a black dot have values where one is double the other.

title: The 79-Cell Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A few months ago Simon tackled a Sneppix sudoku called Grouping All But One - today he tackles the sequel (you can guess the title!) and, with it, Sneppix establishes themselves as a seriously gifted setter. This is original and feels a bit like a discovery - and it deserves at least 10000x the number of solves it's had already!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/28d8kmh1jf

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide all cells in the grid except for r9c7 and r9c9 (the two grey cells) into groups of orthogonally connected cells. Every group contains exactly one cell with a white circle. The digit in a circle cell, N, indicates the number of cells in that group. All cells in a group have the same parity as N. r9c7 and r9c9 are not in any of the groups and may be any digit but are still affected by normal Sudoku rules. As an example, a circle cell containing a 4 is in a group of 4 orthogonally connected cells that are all even. Note: Adjacent cells with the same parity could still be part of different groups; the parity restriction solely affects cells within the same group. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given.

title: Remember NOT To Do Sudoku!! Rat Run 36: Alternating Currant (S3:E16)
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

And you can hear Simon recite the story so far here:
https://youtu.be/kCF9uLrsEus

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty's done it again with this one. Pure madness wrapped up in a 9x9 grid of utter mischief and mayhem! It's called Alternating Currant (what a title!) and it is absolutely essential you don't do sudoku if you want to solve this sudoku!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/jewe3tzhy9

Rules:
SOMEDOKU: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that each row N and column N contain exactly N distinct digits, with the rest of the cells in that row / column being repeats. For example, only 3 distinct digits appear in row 3, and any of these can be repeated multiple times in order to fill the row.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths may only intersect at the cupcake cell.
As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell.
BLACKCURRANTS: If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other.
REDCURRANTS: If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even.
GRAPES: If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5.
CAGES: Digits may not repeat within a cage. Each cage has the same total, to be deduced. If the digit on a cage's electricity symbol is 5 or higher, the cage may not be entered.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, both rats visit the same number of cells. Any pair of cells (one on each path) that are an equal distance from the cupcake cell sum to the digit on the cupcake cell. Thus, both paths combined form a valid 'zipper' line, with Finkz and Phinx at the ends and the cupcake cell in the middle.

title: This CANNOT Be Solved, Can It?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A proper mental workout today from Die Hard and his puzzle, Empty Vessels. At first blush it seems there cannot be enough information for this to have a solution but worry away at it and all sorts of things start to emerge. Original and quite wonderful!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9q82og2xas

Rules:

title: Find The River Through The Sudoku Fog
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We love a good fog-of-war sudoku and that's exactly what we've got tonight from Xenonetix. The puzzle is called Douro and we have to find the river (presumably the Douro) through the grid - it really is a lovely solve and not too tricky despite its 4/5 rating.  Enjoy :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/kbrkvktac9

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. There's a one-cell wide 'river' of orthogonally-connected cells snaking from R9C9 to R1C2 without branching or touching itself orthogonally (but it may touch diagonally). Digits along the 'river' differ by at least 5. All remaining cells are 'land'. 'Bridges' (=) only cross single 'river' cells, and are the sum of the two 'land' cells at each end of the 'bridge' (e.g. if the river cell was a 5, the two land cells could be 2&3 or 1&4). Diagonal 'bridges' only cross 'river' corners. Placing a correct digit will clear fog in its cell, and may also clear fog in other cells.

title: The Genius Of Squashing a 9x9 Sudoku Into a 7x7 Grid
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It is ThePedallingPianist's birthday today and we've had lots of recommendations for puzzles of his to try. His own wish was that we had a go at Leftovers - a quite extraordinary 5/5-rated "Squishdoku". Simon decided to give it a quick go (fully prepared that it might not go well) and then spent the next 100 minutes discovering all sorts of things about this magical puzzle.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9fipkj2wr0

Rules:
Place a digit from 1-9 in each cell of the main 7x7 grid. Digits may not repeat in a row, column or 3x3 box of this grid. The grid contains nine 3x3 boxes, which overlap at the dashed lines. Clues in pills refer to the digits missing from the associated row or column, but pills do not need to be filled. Thick purple pills are X-sum clues, i.e. the digits missing from that row or column can form a 2-digit number, which is the sum of the first X digits from the direction of the pill, where X is the first digit seen. The digits missing from a row with a pill containing a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); The digits missing from a row with a pill containing a white dot are consecutive; The digits missing from a column with a pill containing an X sum to 10.

title: Sudoku ... in Base 3?
description:
Here's where you can try Entropic Ternary by Cassinii: https://sudokupad.app/7gyocv8k7m  
Normal sudoku rules apply.
The digits X and Y in a cage (reading left to right) form a pair of coordinates that point to Row X, Column Y (rXcY). The digit at rXcY is determined as follows:
1. If X or Y is in the entropic set: {1,2,3}, it represents the base-3 digit 0; {4,5,6}, it represents the base-3 digit 1; {7,8,9}, it represents the base-3 digit 2.
2. The entropic base-3 representations of X and Y now form a 2-digit base-3 number (reading left to right still).
3. Convert this number back to base-10, and place this digit at rXcY.
No two cage coordinates point to the same cell.
Digits do not repeat along the negative diagonal (blue line). Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Adjacent digits on an orange line differ by at least 4. If a cage has a small number in the top left, the digits in that cage sum to that number. Digits either side of a white dot are consecutive. On a black dot, one digit is double the other. Digits either side of an X sum to 10. Digits either side of a V sum to 5. A digit on a grey square is even.

title: Can You Complete Sudoku's Triple Crown?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
On the eve of Kennet's 7th birthday, we attempt his father's The Triple Crown sudoku - an absolutely brilliant mash-up of some well known rules. Simon even forgives Kennet's Dad's use of the Disjoint Subset rule - one that has given him kittens in the past :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/7m7iluxxil

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on the thin blue main diagonal. Cells that appear in the same relative position of their 3x3 box may not contain the same digit. So, for example, r5c1 (the middle left cell of its 3x3 box) could not contain the same digit as r8c7 (the middle left cell of its 3x3 box.) Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the cage’s top left corner. Digits on a pink line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. The 3x3 box borders divide the thick blue lines into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.

title: The 9 Teleports! Rat Run 35: Locked Out (S3:E15)
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

And you can hear Simon recite the story so far here:
https://youtu.be/kCF9uLrsEus

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Wednesday's continue to deliver their Christmas presents to all sudoku enthusiasts with the arrival of the new Rat Run - today's is Locked Out, the 35th episode of Marty Sear's epic series. It goes without saying that it's a phenomenal puzzle (even if the Lockout Line rule always terrifies Simon) and does it seem like the story might be reaching a denouement?! 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/s64txn1v6l

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT:
Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell.
BLACKCURRANTS: If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant, one is double the other.
REDCURRANTS: If two digits are joined by a redcurrant, one is odd and the other is even.
TELEPORTS: Entering a teleport will cause a rat to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, for any path segment connecting two teleports, no other cells along the segment may equal either of the two teleport digits at its ends, or lie numerically between them. Eg: if a path segment joins two teleports with the digits 3 and 6, then the other digits along this path segment may not include a 3, 4, 5 or 6.

Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and region. A digit in a circle indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit. A digit in a circle also indicates how many of the up-to nine surrounding cells (including itself) are in the same region as that circle. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to ten. Not all dots and X's are necessarily given.

description:
Here's where you can try There's a Wolf Under There by birthday genius ViKingPrime: https://sudokupad.app/g63hqgbauq 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along a pink line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating values in any order. A black dot separates two cells where one is double the value of the other. Place Werewolf cells into the grid so that there is exactly one Werewolf cell in each row, column and box; each Werewolf cell must contain the digit that matches its Box number (counted from left-to-right, top-to-bottom); the value of a Werewolf cell is unique from other Werewolf cells and is selected from the remaining digits within its box (e.g. if the digit 1 in Box 1 has a value of 4, the digit 2 in Box 2 could have neither a value of 2 nor 4).

title: My Sudoku Is Telling Me Lies!!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's VikingPrime's birthday today and, to celebrate his friend's big day, Marty Sears has made him a puzzle... and not just any puzzle... this puzzle mimics VikingPrime's style and this means it is... devious... deeply devious!!  

It's called Hijinks, it's awesomely clever and also very very smelly!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/2hk0wen7pj

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each line, the hexagon is referred to as 'position 1', the next cell along is 'position 2' and so on. Digits never repeat along a line. PURPLE LINES are thermos. Digits along thermos always increase as you move away from the hexagon. Eg: 24579 would be a valid thermo. TURQUOISE LINES are index lines. On an index line, the digit in the Nth position indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. Eg: 32154 would be a valid index line. The 3 in the 1st position indicates there is a 1 in the 3rd position, and so on. LIGHT BROWN LINES are hitlines. Digits can be in any order on a hitline, but the digit in the hexagon  indicates how many digits along the hitline match their position number. Eg: A hitline might read 27315. The 2 on the hexagon indicates that exactly two digits match their position number; in this case, 3 in the 3rd position and 5 in the 5th position. SHENANIGANS: One of the digits 1-9 (to be determined) is the 'mischief digit.' Every line follows one (AND ONLY ONE) of the three line rules above, but any line containing the mischief digit has been painted the wrong colour. (Any line NOT containing the mischief digit is the correct colour.)

title: Colour Your Sudoku = Solve Your Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Jeff Wajes has made some fantastic puzzles in his "coloured circles" series. This one, Circus Maximus, is absolutely one of, if not, THE best. Wonderfully interesting and clean logic from start to finish. This is a 5/5 difficulty sudoku but one that is just so worth spending time with.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/cg5wlayzuj

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a pink line must form a non-repeating group of consecutive digits, but they may appear in any order along the line. Using red, green, and blue, colour all circles such that: Orthogonally adjacent circles are different colours; and the digit inside a circle appears that many times in circles of that colour.

title: Rectangle Sums: A Wonderful New Sudoku Rule
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's been a week for some brilliant and challenging puzzles. Tonight Simon attempts Rectangle Sums by FIT7Y, which is absolutely in keeping. It's a simple but fascinating ruleset that rewards a little technique and simple arithmetic. This is a great sudoku!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/xqqerfk832

Normal sudoku rules apply. Within the grid there are rectangles. Only the upper left and bottom right corners of the rectangles are shown. Each shown corner corresponds to exactly one rectangle. All digits contained within a rectangle sum to the total given in that rectangle's upper left corner.

title: A Death In Sudoku? Rat Run 34: On Reflection (S3:E14)
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty's done in again with another innovative and fantastic (and emotional!) Rat Run puzzle. This one is called On Reflection and it's rated 3/5 for difficulty... but it isn't THAT easy :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/udyn0tghcs

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. The digit on a grey camera indicates the total SUM of the digits in any visited cells that the camera's lens points towards (before a wall is reached, which blocks vision.) A video camera cell itself may not be entered. In this experiment, all of the low digits in the grid (1s, 2s and 3s) must be visited, but none of the high digits (7s, 8s, and 9s) may be visited. The two rats' paths must be perfect reflections of each other across the positive diagonal (marked with a thin pink line).

You can find Marty's document detailing the story so far at this link:
https://www.patreon.com/posts/155713318
(We did try to host this file on YouTube but it wouldn't let us but the link should work and be free to access.)

title: This Sudoku Contains Secret Maths!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Wow. There is so much to admire and wonder about in tonight's sudoku from DubiousMobius titled Supersonic Slingshots. There are some secrets that might be required to solve this one... do you know them?!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ix1pl0qk4b

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Toroidal Grid: The left edge of the grid wraps around to the right, and the bottom wraps to the top.  Clues outside the grid are duplicates of clues inside the grid. Cells separated by a white dot are consecutive.  If two digits are separated by a black dot then one is double the other. 
Supersonic Slingshots: Each slingshot will launch a copy of the digit in the cell directly in front of it (just beyond the sling end) somewhere in the grid.  The digits on a slingshot represent the distance the digit in that cell will travel from its current position.  Multi-cell slingshots have multi-digit values, where the digits are read in Western reading order (so the rightmost or bottommost cell contains the unit digit, its neighbour contains the tens digit, and so on). The flung digit will move forward along its row or column, away from the slingshot's handle.  Upon reaching the grid border, the digit will wrap back around and start flying down its row/column again. For example, if r3c789 were 436 then the digit 4 would be fired to the left 36 cells.

title: Solve the Pirate's Map!
description:
Here's where you can try The Lost Killer Islands by Patrick Junke: https://sudokupad.app/gssntzkary 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells are either 'sea' or 'land'. No 2x2 block is filled with just sea or land. All sea cells are connected orthogonally. Cells with arrows are dead ends, that is, sea cells that point to the only other sea cell they touch. 
Land cells form 'islands' that don't touch each other, even diagonally, comprising four orthogonally adjacent, different digits, summing to 14. On an X, the two digits sum to 10, and on a red dot, they sum to 12. All arrows, X's, and red dots are shown. On an X, the two cells are both sea or both land.

title: "Sudoku Expert" Gets Owned....
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Oh dear, oh dear... Simon saw a new zetamath & friends puzzle on Logic Masters and thought 'oh, that sounds like a good sudoku to try at 4.30pm in the afternoon...' Well, on this and many other things, Simon was badly wrong! This is probably quite a tricky puzzle and, if you're going to attempt it, make sure you have your correct brain in....!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yvkb4l2c2j

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each letter from ABCDEFGHZ stands for a different digit from 1-9.  Each labeled gray letter cell in the grid contains that digit.  Where a ? is used, it always represents a two digit total.  Ie the leading question mark is never 0. Digits in cages sum to the total given.  Digits cannot repeat within cages. Digits along indicated diagonals have the indicated sum.  Digits may repeat along such diagonals. Circles within the grid are quadruples.  The indicated digit appears in at least one of the four surrounding cells. Digits with a door are numbered rooms.  The indicated digit appears a number of cells into that row or column given by the first number in that row/column. Digits with a building are skyscrapers.  They indicate how many digits are seen from the perspective of the clue if digits are only seen if they are the highest digit encountered so far.

title: Dividing Small Integers By 3 = FASCINATING!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Michael Lefkowitz is one of the most creative minds in the world of puzzles and he's come up with something truly weird and wonderful called Modularrows. The idea is incredibly simple but the implications are far from obvious (but it's so satisfying when you find them!)
[Don't forget to check out our new app featuring the puzzles of Blobz! Details below.]

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/nozibzvmcc

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. MODULAR ARROWS: A digit on an arrow counts how many cells in the indicated direction have the same remainder mod-3 as itself, including itself. title: Carry On Solving!
description:
Here's where you can try Schrödinger's Carry-on by James Sinclair: https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/schrodingers-carry-on?setting-nogrid=1 
Fill each row, column, and box with the digits 0-6 once each. Exactly one cell in each row, column, and box is a "Schrödinger's cell," which contains two digits. Two Schrödinger's cells cannot contain the same pair of digits.
A cell's value is equal to the sum of its digits. For final solution check purposes, if a cell's value is from 0-9, enter the *digit* equal to its value; otherwise, the cell may be left empty (in-progress solution-checking doesn't work properly in this puzzle).
Cells with red squares are index cells. If an index cell in column X has a value of Y, then the cell in column Y in the same row has a value of X (e.g. if r3c1 has a value of 5, then r3c5 has a value of 1). An index cell may contain two digits, but may not have a value greater than 6. If an index cell has a value of zero, the value being indexed does not appear in the row. Nothing in these rules prevents a value from repeating in a row, even if one instance of that value is referenced by an index cell.
The sum of the values along an arrow is equal to the value in the connected circle.

title: Absolute Puzzle Genius! Rat Run 33: Hot And Cold (S3:E13)
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Every Wednesday is like Christmas if you're a sudoku fan at the moment with the latest puzzle in Marty Sears' Rat Run series arriving in our in-boxes! To be this inventive every single week is simply not normal and yet Marty delivers each and every time. This is another AMAZING rat run and Simon is very grateful he left room for Notes :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/dqu2xb1itj

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls.
HOT AND COLD ZONES: Divide the grid into two zones of orthogonally connected cells, one hot and the other cold. No 2x2 area may be completely in one zone. 
INVISIBLE WALLS:  A few maze walls are visible, but the rest are invisible and must be located. If two orthogonally adjacent cells are in different zones, a wall exists between them. If they are in the same zone, no wall exists between them. Because no 2x2 spaces exist fully within one zone, no diagonal movements are possible in this maze.
BOX BALANCE:
• The value of a hot cell equals its digit +1.
• The value of a cold cell equals its digit -1.
• In each 3x3 box, the total value of hot cells must equal the total value of cold cells.
CURRANTS:
• If a BLACKCURRANT sits between two cells, then the value of one is double the value of the other. 
• If a REDCURRANT sits between two cells, then one has an odd value and the other has an even value.
• Two cells joined by a currant are both in the same zone.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, Phinx must stay in the hot zone and Finkz must stay in the cold zone.

title: All in All, it's just another Brick in the Wall
description:
Here's where you can try Wallfacer by M.K.: https://sudokupad.app/uz9llk6x4x 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered with fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. On a black dot one digit is double the other. Draw a 1-cell wide "wall" that divides the grid such that the white dots are separated from the black dots. The wall cannot branch or touch itself (even diagonally). Dots can touch the wall, but they can't be on top of it. Digits that share an edge with the wall are at least 4 lower than their orthogonal neighbors on the wall. Adjacent digits on the wall are consecutive.

title: Is This Sudoku Of Average Difficulty...? I DON'T THINK SO!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A completely fascinating sudoku tonight from oskode called Count Me In which combines counting circles-type logic with loop building. There seems to be no concensus in terms of how hard this puzzle really is: we've had it requested by people who have got stuck on it; but some say it's relatively straightforward... You can probably tell from the video length what Simon thinks!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/bs3y9058h7

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell wide loop in the grid, passing through the centres of some orthogonally adjacent cells. The loop does not touch itself, not even diagonally. A digit on the loop indicates how many times that digit appears on the loop. A digit in a cell containing an arrow counts how many loop cells are in the indicated direction (not including the cell with the arrow). Multiple arrows in the same cell count loop cells independent of one another (so if r6c4 is a 3 then there are three loop cells to its north and three loop cells to its north east).

title: New Lines for Mathematicians!
description:
Here's where you can try Red Light, Green Light by Hanks: https://sudokupad.app/vriogscu49 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Entering a correct digit clears fog in its cell, and may or may not clear fog in other cells.
All digits on a red (triangle inequality) line are distinct. Furthermore, any three (not necessarily adjacent!) distinct digits {x,y,z} on a red line satisfy the Triangle Inequality, i.e., x+y= more than z, y+z= more than x, and z+x= more than y.
All digits on a green line are distinct. Furthermore, any three (not necessarily adjacent!) distinct digits {a,b,c} on a green line do not satisfy the Triangle Inequality, i.e., the sum of the two smaller digits in {a,b,c} is less than or equal to the largest digit in {a,b,c}.

title: Minesweeper: Japanese-style!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for rdrd and their (very original) puzzle Japanese Minesweeper (Beginner). Don't worry if you fear it'll be too easy... we don't think it is! It is however clever and interesting - which basically makes it ideal for the channel!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/acruau5lrz

Rules:
Minesweeper: There are 10 mines in the grid. Every clued cell (i.e., a non-mine cell that is orthogonally or diagonally adjacent to at least one mine) contains a digit equal to the number of adjacent mines. Cells not adjacent to any mine are left empty. Japanese Sums: Clues outside the grid represent the (non-zero) sum of digits in each contiguous sequence of clued cells, in the order of appearance from left to right or top to bottom. Consecutive sequences must be separated by at least one mine cell or one empty cell. A ? represents a one-digit number and a ?? represents a two-digit number. (For solution checking, in addition to the numbers you've entered above, enter 9 to indicate a cell with a mine and 0 for cells with zero adjacent mines).

No region contains more than one circled cell. Not all regions contain a circle. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. title: The April Fool Sudoku! Rat Run 32 Veracity (S3:E12)
description:
As mentioned in the video introduction, Marty has designed some incredible Rat Run merchandise:

https://cracking-the-cryptric-shop.fourthwall.com/en-gbp/collections/rat-run

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy April Fools Day. It seems Marty Sears wanted to make sure we all knew it was All Fools Day too because this is one of the most brilliant, funny and wonderful Rat Run sudokus ever - and that's saying quite something. Why can't the rats just go to the cupcakes that are almost next to them? And just what is going on!?

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/o2u3rfkurb

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. No diagonal moves are possible in this maze. If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant, one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a redcurrant, one is odd and the other is even. If two digits are joined by a goldenberry, they are non-consecutive. If two digits are joined by a grape, they have a difference of at least 5. A digit on a motion sensor indicates exactly how many cells in the (up to 9) surrounding cells are visited by a rat. In this experiment, some clues are fake! (A fake clue breaks its rule in the list above.) All clues that Phinx passes through are fake. All other clues are truthful (ie; those passed through by Finkz, and those unvisited by either rat.) It is to be determined which rat is which.

Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage must sum to a unique triangular number (1,3,6,10,15,21,...). title: The Beautiful Islands of Sudoku!
description:
Please note that Monday's stream will start at 5pm Eastern Time. In Europe the clocks have changed.
Here's where you can try Archipelago by Lithium-Ion: https://sudokupad.app/uy0r96nw2i 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cell in the grid belongs to exactly one terrain: Either island (green) or water (blue). All water cells in the grid must form one orthogonally connected region. Each 2x2 region in the grid contains at least one cell from each terrain. Each island contains exactly one clue, which equals the product of the size of the island (i.e. the number of cells that belong to this island) and the sum of the digits in all cells belonging to this island. Digits within an island do not repeat. Islands are not allowed to touch each other (neither orthogonally nor diagonally). A digit in a circle equals the size of the island. Not all possible circles are given.

title: The Royal Albert Hall: A Sudoku Tribute
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today marks the 155th birthday of one of London's most famous buildings: The Royal Albert Hall! It was opened by Queen Victoria as a memorial to her late husband Prince Albert in 1871 and is world-renowned as a concert venue par excellence and home of the BBC Proms. We're celebrating the birthday with a special puzzle created by ThePedallingPianist, who rather aptly has himself appeared in 5 Proms! He's created a wonderful sudoku puzzle in and of itself but the theming is fantastic too - even including the appearance of the "mushrooms" that hang from the Hall's ceiling. Enjoy.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/x0xwsud0hq

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The blue "R" is split by a box border into two segments whose digits have the same sum. Each pair of adjacent digits on the red "A" must contain one odd and one even digit. Each pair of adjacent digits on the green "H" must have a difference of at least 5. A digit on a Fibreglass Acoustic Diffuser (mushroom) shows how many times that digit appears on Fibreglass Acoustic Diffusers. For each Fibreglass Acoustic Diffuser, digits may not echo (repeat) in the up to 4 orthogonally adjacent cells.

title: How Can This Possibly Work??!! Rat Run 31: Equivalence (S3:E11)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
For the first time ever in the history of Rat Run, Marty Sears has teamed up with another setter, Justin Vitanza, to produce an extraordinary sudoku with a ruleset that seems absolutely crazy at first glance. This might be the hardest Rat Run ever too - it has a 5/5 difficulty rating but it's hard to think of a better way to spend your puzzling time. It's simply fantastic.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/37wqeifgzs

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. Entering a yellow teleport will cause a rat to be instantly transported to the other yellow teleport. The teleports have identical digits. The digit on a pink motion sensor indicates the number of cells that are visited (by either rat) within the (up to 9) cells immediately surrounding the sensor. The sensor itself is counted, if visited. In this experiment, for any row or column, the digits visited by Finkz must have the same sum as the digits visited by Phinx. This sum must be determined for each row and column.

title: Psycho: The Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

title: Two Truths And A Lie: Fog Sudoku Goes Absolutely Mad!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the most bizarre and, frankly, amazing "2 truths and a lie" sudokus we've ever seen tonight from gdc. It's called '2 Truths And A Region' and it sets a series of almost discrete challenges that all seem utterly intractable!!  If you choose to try it, let us know how you got on!! Good Luck :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/4ssf9qr9l9

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 𝗗𝘆𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗰 𝗙𝗼𝗴 hides some clues. Placing a correct digit clears fog from its cell and possibly other cells. For each clue type listed below, there are three clues of that type in the grid which don't share cells. Two of them are correct, and one is incorrect ('lying'). For each clue type, all cells clued by that type (incl. the liar) contain different digits. 𝗖𝗹𝘂𝗲 𝗧𝘆𝗽𝗲𝘀: 1) 𝗖𝗮𝗴𝗲𝘀: Digits in a cage sum to the total in the top-left. 2) 𝗩: Each V joins two digits that sum to 5. 3) 𝗗𝗼𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗔𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀 (DA): If two circles in different cells are connected by a line, the sum in the circles is equal to the sum of the remaining (0+ cell) line. 4) 𝗔𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀 (A): Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. 5) 𝗥𝗲𝗻𝗯𝗮𝗻 (R): Digits on a hollow line form a single consecutive sequence (like 234) in any order. 6) If two digits are joined by a black dot then one is double the other.

title: Put a little Birdlife in your Sudoku
description:
For anyone wondering where Wordle in a Minute is today, it has been recorded but I won't be able to get it onto YouTube until late tomorrow (after the next one has come out)!. Sorry!
Here's where you can try Ornithological Adjacency by Jrosas: https://sudokupad.app/n2v6rs916k 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Across the white dot the two digits are consecutive.
Some orthogonally adjacent cells are separated by birds. Each bird indicates a specific ratio. All pairs of digits on the same kind of bird are in an equal ratio eg. a pelican might lie between pairs of digits that share a 3:4 ratio. If so, the ornithologically related pairs across pelicans would be 3:4, 6:8, 4:3, and 8:6. Not all possible birds are given.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon hasn't tried a sudoku by NurglesGift before but he gets to try EXclusiVe tonight and a VERY fine puzzle it is too - with one of our favourite rule twists!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/aixxhbtkvj

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The following constraints operate in this puzzle: 1) Cells connected by an X must sum to 10; 2) Cells connected by an V must sum to 5; 3) Digits in a cage sum to the small number in the cage's top-left corner; 4) Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle; and 5) Digits on a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Within any single constraint type listed above, digits may not repeat.  (Eg If one caged cell contained a 1, no other caged cell anywhere in the puzzle can contain a 1.)

title: Modular Yin Yang
description:
Here's where you can attempt Modular Yin Yang by Yttrio: https://sudokupad.app/yttrio/modular-yin-yang 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. A digit in a cell with an arrow counts the total number of shaded cells seen in the direction of the arrow (not counting the cell itself).
For every 2x2 area in the puzzle, no two shaded cells can be from the same modulo 3 set. In other words, in any given 2x2 area, there can only be one shaded cell with a digit from [147], one from [258], and one from [369].

title: Sudoku's Dutch Fog!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tim Hasselaar is a relatively new name in the world of sudoku construction and this is Simon's first chance to try one of Tim's puzzles. It's called Dutch Summer and it's a fog-of-war sudoku and some excellent and surprising logic. This one is a lot of fun if you give it a chance!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/hrsm0gqb5o

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply

It's summer in the Netherlands! Unfortunately that still means there's a high chance of bad weather, and thus fog.

Unique to the Dutch summer, the (orange) 'dutch whisper' lines are also region sum lines. ie 1) Adjacent digits along the a line must differ in value by at least 4; and 2) the 3x3 box borders divide each line into segments; the segments along an individual line must each have the same sum. 

Additionally, every 2x2 square of cells must contain a low digit (1,2,3); a middle digit (4,5,6); and a high digit (7,8,9). Placing a correct digit might clear extra fog. Guessing is not required.

title: The Extending Palindromes!! Rat Run 30: Star Rats (S3:E10)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty dazzles us again this evening with Episode 10 of the latest (and last) Rat Run season. It's called Star Rats and the title alludes to the fact that somehow the rats' paths need to form a gigantic palindrome! Fantastic!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/axfuqiprqj

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths may not share cells except for where they meet at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. There is one booster cell in every row, column and box, and each contains a different digit. The value of a booster cell equals its digit, plus its row number, plus its column number. Eg: If r7c3 is a booster cell and contains a 6, it will have a value of 16 (7+3+6). If two cells are joined by a blackcurrant then the value of one is double the value of the other. The sum of the two values joined by a starfruit is always the same, and must be deduced. In this experiment, both rats visit the same number of cells, and the sequence of VALUES along both paths are identical. Eg: If the first five values visited by Finkz are 7, 4, 12, 3, 8 (in that order) then the same must be true for Phinx.

title: Haunted by a Tough Sudoku
description:
Here's where you can attempt (if you dare) Haunted Mansion by Eccentric Panda: https://sudokupad.app/l01qpi8oc3 
Divide the grid into 9 orthogonally connected rooms. Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and room. Find a path that travels orthogonally through the haunted mansion and does not revisit cells. Start at the entry (R8, C9), and end at the ghost in the attic (R3, C9). The path may only pass through room walls where there is a door (brown line). Doors are always on walls, never in the middle of a room. 
Digits on ghosts are all different. The digit on a ghost counts how many cells of its room can be seen horizontally and vertically including itself. Walls block vision. The path visits all the ghosts. The temperature (digits) decreases if you step toward a ghost in the room you’re in and increases if you step away, including if you re-enter a room. A ghost will always have the lowest digit on the path in its room. No need to take temperature readings if you enter a room without a ghost, digits on those paths will be random.
If you enter a secret passage (hole emoji), you will exit from a different passage with the same digit. Each passage shares exactly one other passage with the same digit. Digits on either side of a bat are in a 1:3 ratio.

We've had a few recommendations and requests to tackle this remarkable puzzle by Las4one called FUll Rankillers. It's had very few solves and this might be because it is VERY VERY HARD!! What does Simon make of it?!

https://sudokupad.app/kh62gdjsgt

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply within the central 9x9 area. 
Full Rank: The digits in columns and rows, read in both directions, make a total of 36 nine-digit numbers. Cells outside the grid have a value equal to the rank in ascending order among those 36 numbers for the indicated column or row in the direction of the cell. Digits may not repeat within a cage. A double-digit clue inside of a cage prevents both of its digits from appearing anywhere else in the same cage (this means 11, 22 and 33 may not appear in a cage, and 8 and 18, for example, may not appear in the same cage). Here's where you can try The Mystery Of The Three Chameleons by The Pi Guy: https://sudokupad.app/5or0u7cv0o 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits 7, 8 and 9 (the chameleons) have a value equal to their row (for 7), column (for 8) or box (for 9).
The values on an arrow adds to the value in the attached circle. On a black dot, one value is double the other. Every neighbouring pair of cells along a green line contains values that are at least 5 apart. The values on a purple line must be a consecutive sequence in some order, with no repeats.

title: Just About Everybody Loves This Sudoku!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears makes great sudoku puzzles. We've been enjoying his Rat Run Season 3 extravaganazas in the middle of the week but, occasionally, we don't like it to stop there! Dutch Flat Mates: Split Ends uses a ruleset we think Marty invented and it's a relatively approachable puzzle packed full of v nice logic :) Happy Mothers Day!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/n44kqgll5s

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. Each horizontal blonde line sums to a 2 digit number. These two digits are at the start and end of its row, in some order. Each vertical brunette line also sums to a 2 digit number. These two digits are at the top and bottom of its column, in some order.

title: Another Candidate For The Sudoku Museum
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Fool On Hill is an amazing solver but we've only rarely solved one of the sudokus he's set. Tonight Simon tried Dancing In A Ring, which seemed set up to remind us of some techniques we once knew... 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/b37xfe4xjf

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green German Whisper line differ by at least 5. Digits on a pink Renban line form a consecutive set with no repeats. The central cross is a single line. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Where digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. title: If There Was A Sudoku Museum, This Should Be In It. Rat Run 29: Counterbalance (S3:E9)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
If the World of Sudoku ever has a museum (Simon likes this idea!) then this puzzle should be an exhibit in it. Marty Sears' latest Rat Run - Counterbalance (possibly the penultimate puzzle in this Season?) is simply one of the most imaginative and brilliant sudokus you'll ever solve. Dazzling.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/xipcvuhz9y

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. A purple arrow may only be passed through in the direction it's pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. In this experiment, any digit on Finkz' path indicates exactly how many times that digit appears on Finkz' path. The same rule applies separately for Phinx' path.

title: When The Fog Clears, The Sudoku Rules Change...!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Nurator's latest fog-of-war sudoku is absolutely fantastic - even a slightly-under-the-weather Simon has a blast solving this one and making his way from checkpoint to checkpoint!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/iovwq0jc5n

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one digit is double the other. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given. Deducing the digit in the highest visible checkpoint (marked with a green square and a number) will reveal new cells and potentially a new checkpoint. Each line follows the rules of one specific constraint type from the following list. It is up to the solver to determine which line belongs to which type. Each line constraint type may contain NO REPEATED DIGITS anywhere in the puzzle. At the start of the puzzle, all lines are Region Sum Lines (ie the 3x3 box borders divide the lines into segments; each segment along an individual line has the same sum). When a new checkpoint is revealed, remove the determined line types and all entered digits EXCEPT those on checkpoints. You are now allowed a new line constraint! Checkpoint 1: Additionally, the lines can now be German Whisper lines (Adjacent digits differ by at least 5) Checkpoint 2: Additionally, the lines can now be Parity lines (Digits alternate between odd and even digits) You have completed the puzzle when all 3 checkpoints are revealed and the complete grid is filled.

title: Henry the Horse Jumps Through the Fog!
description:
Here's where you can try Horsing Around by Tim Hasselaar: https://sudokupad.app/3di357jqj1 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing a correct digit might remove some fog.
Henry the horse wants to jump around the sudoku grid. He can only do this by jumping from number to number with a chess knight's move. On his journey through the grid he will jump on every instance of his favorite number, the number 1. The only other number he can jump on is a 5, but never twice in a row. Henry can't jump over blue walls, but he can jump around them if a knight's move allows it. Henry's journey starts on the green circle, (either 1 or 5), and ends when he jumps on the 9th instance of his favorite number. Henry cannot jump to a cell he's already visited.
Every pair of consecutive cells along the red line must contain both an even and an uneven number. A cell with arrows pointing inwards is smaller than all orthogonally adjacent cells. On a black dot, one digit is double the other.

title: Numberphile Math Guy Returns With A Crazy Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
MathGuy_12 is one of very few sudoku constructors to have had one of their sudokus featured in a @numberphile episode. His latest, Xerox, builds on some of the logic we saw in Marty Sears' 6x6 sudoku on Friday but how will it work in a 9x9?! "Amazingly well!", it turns out!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/9qw21nnjuy

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. All the 2x2 areas of the grid, when read in normal reading order, make a total of 64 four-digit numbers.  Clues in the centre of a 2x2 area show its rank among those 64 numbers, where the lowest is 1 and the highest is 64. The two “X”s are the same number. One or more equal numbers are considered to be at rank N when there are N-1 numbers of strictly lower rank. (Eg, if there are three equal numbers which have 19 numbers lower than them then these three numbers would be rank 20 and the next rank will be 23, i.e. the ranks could go ⋯, 19, 20, 20, 20, 23, ⋯)

title: The Miracle 6x6 Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've been loving the 3rd season of Rat Run by Marty Sears but tonight we attempt Ranked Quads, a new sudoku from the great man with a completely original ruleset (for us at least). It is close to astonishing that just four quad clues resolve this one uniquely and yet it only has a 2/5 difficulty rating. This is a very special puzzle.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/0oajbse81h

Rules:
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1-6, once each, into every row, column and 2x3 rectangle). Each digit in a circle must appear in the surrounding 2x2 area. (If a digit appears twice in the circle it must appear twice in the 2x2 area.) The 25 2x2 areas in the grid each contain a 4-digit number (reading from top left to bottom right.) The number in a circle gives the rank of its surrounding 2x2 area, if all these 4-digit numbers are listed from lowest to highest, with rank 1 being the lowest and rank 25 being the highest. All the 4-digit numbers are different, so there are no tied ranks.

title: The Einstein Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A real innovation today in which Synergenesis & mbumbee, two new constructors, who have combined sudoku with an Einstein puzzle (often called a Logic Puzzle in the UK). This probably won't be a regular item simply because of the amount of space necessary on the screen but, as a one-off, we have to commend the pair on a really fantastic experience - it's not easy but the way the two puzzles work together is lovely.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/dyg2otjpgb
and the Logic puzzle is available here:
https://tinyurl.com/2sh9dc7b
(For those without tinyurl abilities we've included the full link in a comment under the video.)

Rules:
This puzzle combines sudoku and an Einstein puzzle or logic grid. Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a V sum to 5 and cells separated by an X sum to 10. Cells along a green line are at least 5 apart. Cells along a purple line are consecutive numbers, in some order. On a thermometer, digits increase from the bulb. Cells along an arrow sum to the value in the connected circle. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one is double the other. One of the four cells touching the circle containing a 9 contains the digit 9. In addition, every sudoku digit has a unique favourite colour and a unique favourite shape. Colours are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, brown, and silver. Shapes are circle, triangle, square, star, diamond, heart, crescent, cross, and pentagon. A digit will only share a cell with its favourite colour and/or shape. The following 6 clues and the sudoku grid will allow you to determine each digit's favourite colour and shape. 
1. The digit one's favourite shape is not a heart. 
2. There are four digits whose value is equal to the number of letters in their favourite colour; 
3. The digit whose favourite colour is yellow has the star as their favourite shape; 
4. The pentagon is the favourite shape of an even digit; 
5. The digit whose favourite colour is silver is greater than six; 
6. The digit whose favourite colour is purple is never orthogonally adjacent to two of the same number at once. 
For clarity, r9c2 is a pink cell. Also, the circles in the thermometer and arrow are not shapes for the purposes of solving the puzzle. A true circle is displayed in r4c5.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely beautiful and brilliant new Rat Run sudoku tonight from the unbelievably inventive Marty Sears. This one is called Hypothesis and it solves every bit as wonderfully as it looks!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ydgn4bxilt

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Entering a teleport will cause a rat to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. A purple arrow may only be passed through in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between. A green grape sits between two digits with a difference of at least 5. In this experiment, Finkz may only visit even digits, and Phinx may only visit odd digits. You must determine which rat is which.

title: The Hardest 2/5 Difficulty Sudoku!!
description:
(Pls note that Simon's volume may be slightly low tonight - he's realised the problem and it should be better tomorrow but apologies if the balance is a little low this evening.) 

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for Rab3aron and their sudoku Spreading Through The Fog. This is a spectacular puzzle too with some highly original logical ideas unpinning it. It is also rated 2/5 for difficulty on Logic Masters but Simon finds it MUCH harder than that. Is he being daft? 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/f4ec7xtau8

Rules:
Divide the grid into 9 non-overlapping regions, each consisting of orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1–9 exactly once in each row, column, and region. A digit in a circle equals the number of distinct columns occupied by its region. There are 9 circles in total, and exactly one pair of circles share the same digit. A digit in a square equals the number of distinct rows occupied by its region. There are 9 squares in total, and exactly one pair of squares share the same digit. A digit in a diamond equals the number of distinct regions that appear anywhere in its row or column, including its own region (regions seen in both the row and column are still counted once). The sum of every circled and squared digit within a region is the same for each of the nine regions. The grid is covered in fog, placing correct digits clears the fog somewhere in the grid.

title: Who Is Hidden In The Sudoku Fog?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely charming fog-of-war sudoku tonight from Knightemaire and a puzzle created to celebrate the birth of their nephew, Simon, on 3 February. We're attempting this on the constructor's birthday, which also happens to be Simon's mother's Chelsea's birthday too! 

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/6uqtssso3q

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog conceals part of the puzzle. When some digits are correctly entered, some of the fog may be lifted. Digits along an arrow must sum to the two-digit number formed by the digits in the pill. Adjacent cells along a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Adjacent cells along an orange line must have a difference of at least 4. Every pair of consecutive cells along a red line must contain an odd and even digit. Digits along a pink line must form a consecutive set in any order. Digits in a cage must sum to the number in the cage’s top-left corner. Cells joined by a white dot must be consecutive. If two digits are joined by a black dot, one digit must be double the other.

title: White To Play And Mate In 1. Er, What?!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A completely original and utterly brilliant SUDOKU today from masetab called Chess-doku - a good name seeing as we have to achieve mate in 1! We suspect a little bit of chess knowledge may be essential to solve this but we're not complaining, this is epic!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/p4f84nlzhv

Rules:
Normal 8×8 sudoku rules apply. Each circled cell represents a chess piece on the corresponding square of a chessboard, with White moving up the board. Each piece type and colour is assigned a unique digit (eg all white pawns share one digit and all black pawns another), and not all piece types must appear. All white pieces are globally lower digits than all black pieces ((i.e. the highest white piece is lower than the lowest black piece), and within each colour the digit values follow standard chess hierarchy if they exist: Pawn is less than Knight is less than Bishop is less than Rook is less than Queen is less than King. The chess position is legal, no piece is currently attacking any piece of the opposite colour, regardless of it is defended, and White and Black have identical material (the same number of each piece type). No pawn promotions have occurred. It is White to move, and White has a checkmate in one. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The new season of Rat Run continues tonight with Productivity and this one is seriously challenging. It's also absolutely brilliant and Simon goes to every effort to ensure his whole path is logical... even if he realises halfway through he might need to correct his course...

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/syu6xcezzm

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If two digits are joined by a goldenberry, they are NOT consecutive. In this experiment, both paths are divided into segments by 3x3 box borders. Along a path, the digits on each segment have the same product (the result of multiplying the digits on the segment together.) This product may be different for Finkz and Phinx. title: The Sudoku With Invisible Clues!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Dorlir is a maths professor and today Simon attempts his puzzle Quadratics, which is one of the more mathsy sudokus we've seen. For all that (and Simon's lack of faith in his memory of school mathematics) this is one of those unforgettable puzzles that we're lucky enough to battle with from time to time on the channel. Quite quite unique!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/wobk83t65m

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each circle contains four invisible digits (not necessarily distinct and to be deduced). These must each appear in the surrounding four cells. Quadratics: Of the four digits on a circle, two of them are the two solutions of X^2 - aX + b = 0, where a & b are the other two digits on that circle. If the equation has only one solution, that digit is repeated twice.

title: The Elements of Modified Sudoku
description:
Here's where you can try Fire and Water by Mad-Tyas: https://sudokupad.app/kglg9thtij
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are nine Fire cells in the grid, exactly one in each row, column and marked 3x3 box and filled with a complete set of the digits 1-9. There also are nine Water cells following the same rules as the Fire Cells. It's possible for a cell to belong to both sets simultaneously. The value of Fire and Water cells is the digit in the cell multiplied by the minimum number of orthogonal steps between the Fire cell and the Water cell within the respective marked 3x3 box. If a cell is Fire and Water cell at the same time, its value is 0 cause the minimum number of orthogonal steps is 0. In cages marked with a black dashed line digits must not repeat and the values have to add up to the total given in the top-left corner of a cage.
Note: As the same rules apply to the set of Fire cells and the set of Water cells, it's not possible or required to decide which of the sets is Fire and which is Water.

title: Marty's New Sudoku Maze! Rat Run 26: Hit And Miss (S3:E6)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The new season of Rat Run continues tonight with Hit And Miss (Number 26 in this incredible series). Finkz and Phinx are on top form today with an amazing test constrain that's just classic Marty Sears!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/k4zgmts5h9

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths may not share cells except where they meet at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If two digits are separated by a blackcurrant, one is double the other. If two digits are separated by a grape, they have a difference of at least 5. In this experiment, 3x3 box borders divide both rats' paths up into segments. Not all blue hexagonal platforms need to be visited, but any blue platform that does gets stepped on becomes a 'hit counter'; its digit will indicate exactly how many digits along its path segment match their position number (the first cell visited along a segment is 'position 1'.) Eg: If Finkz visits the digits 97325 (in that order) along a segment, then the 2 would be on its blue hit counter, because two digits match their position number; 3 is visited 3rd and 5 is visited 5th.

title: Humanity Strikes Back! Beating AI At Its Own Game...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Yesterday we attempted a puzzle called Spotlight Fracture which had been created by Claude Opus 4.6 from a single AI prompt. title: AI Was Asked To Create A Modern Sudoku... (Tech/AI Breakthrough)
description:
AI Creates New Type Of Sudoku...
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We aren't quite sure how to feel about this... Thoughtbyte, whose puzzles we've featured many times on the channel, has been testing AI models upon their release to see whether any could create a modern variant sudoku. This hasn't been successful at all... until yesterday Claude Opus 4.6 (Extended Thinking) received the following prompt:

"please create a 6x6 chaos construction sudoku with a novel rule set such that the grid has no given digits but it can be solved logically buy a human"

and it did exactly as asked. We present Spotlight Fracture by Claude Opus 4.6 along with the question: Is it any good?

title: How Can This Sudoku Possibly Solve?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely amazing sudoku tonight from Sneppix (a new name to us) called Grouping All But One. It's a puzzle with so much depth and some fascinating underlying ideas... however it's probably not easy... See how you go!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/xyib4cu1cz

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide all cells in the grid except for r9c7 (the grey cell) into groups of orthogonally connected cells. Every group contains exactly one cell with a white square. The digit in a square cell, N, indicates the number of cells in that group. N will either be the largest or the smallest digit in its group, and digits within a group may not repeat. r9c7 is not in any of the groups and may be any digit, but is still affected by normal sudoku rules. As an example, a square cell containing a 4 is in a group of 4 orthogonally connected cells consisting of unique digits that are all either at most 4 or at least 4. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive and are in different groups.

title: How Can A Sudoku Maze Do This?!! Rat Run 25! (S3:E5)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The new season of Rat Run continues to wow us all tonight with Episode 25, Mod Cons. Marty's brain has added video cameras to the picture and it's fair to say that Phinx and Finkz are intent on taking the most bizarre paths to their treats ;)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/z3tyv4nda6

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits then one is double the other. Finkz and Phinx may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between. The digit on a pink motion sensor indicates the number of cells that are visited within the (up to 9) cells immediately surrounding the sensor. The sensor itself is counted, if visited. The digit on a grey camera indicates the total SUM of the digits in any visited cells that the camera's lens points towards (before a wall is reached, which blocks vision.) In this experiment, both paths are valid 'modular lines'. Any set of 3 successive cells along a path contain one digit from each of the groups [1,4,7], [2,5,8] and [3,6,9].

title: This Is Quite Simply Sudoku Art
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Yesterday's fireworks were always going to be a tough act to follow but a new setter (to us at least), Juho Snellman, has made an incredible deconstruction sudoku themed on the work of Mondrian! It's called Mondrian's Revenge and we've never seen anything quite like it. It's challenging but absolutely incredible.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/xh8xv5itva

Rules:
Place 9 non-overlapping 3x3 boxes in the grid. Place the digits 1-9 in each box. Digits may not repeat in a box, row, or column. For the avoidance of doubt, 0 is not to be entered in any cell. Draw a straight vertical or horizontal line through each circle. The lines may not overlap, and there must be exactly one circle on each line. The digit in the circle is the length of the line going through that circle (a line of length 1 covers 1 cell and does not leave the circle cell, length 2 covers 2 cells, etc). None of the digits 1-9 will appear in circles the same number of times. (At most one digit may appear zero times). Adjacent cells marked with a white dot have consecutive digits. Adjacent cells marked with a black dot indicate one digit is double the other digit. Not all possible dots are given.

title: The Most Extraordinary Sudoku In YEARS
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Mark was so convinced Simon would be blown away by tonight's sudoku that he asked him to open it live on camera. It's a Kaktuslav puzzle called Forcing but it's also mad. Despite being a "chaos construction" (ie a sudoku whose 9-cell regions can be any shape and need to be discovered rather than given as 3x3 boxes), the ruleset is just a single paragraph long. This has been hewn out of nature itself and is surely one of the most remarkable constructions we've ever showcased.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/jcdh680q0f

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine non-overlapping regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1–9 once each in every row, column, and region. In each region, place a circle in the leftmost cell of its topmost row. Every circled digit counts how many cells of its own region (including itself) are visible in its column (region borders block the view). The nine circled cells together form an extra region, i.e. they are orthogonally connected and contain the digits 1–9 once each.

title: The 9th Symphony Of Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We know very little about this sudoku apart from it's only the second puzzle constructed by Timpanist, who is a French Horn player!! What we have since discovered is that this is a bit of a masterpiece. A really fascinating ruleset and an even more fascinating solve.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/185kxmxozs

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single closed loop that moves orthogonally and does not branch or intersect itself. The loop must visit every cell except for the nine cells containing a 9. The 3x3 box borders divide the loop into segments. Within a box, every segment must have the same sum. (This sum may vary from box to box). Every box must have at least two segments. No two adjacent cells directly connected by the loop may sum to 9.

title: That Is One Strange-Looking Sudoku!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We remember MathGuy_12's first puzzle - which was featured in a Numberphile video! His latest is a sudoku/fillomino hybrid that's had some very strong recommendations in the last 48 hours. Unsurprisingly this is with good reason! It's a fascinating puzzle with some unusual and lovely ideas at its heart.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/420l0gdv0c

Rules:
Numbers may not repeat within cages. Within the inner 5x5 grid: Place the digits 1 to 5 such that digits do not repeat in any row or column. Considering all rows and columns as 5-digit numbers read from the direction of the clue and ranked from lowest (1) to highest (20), a clue cell represents where in the ranking that row/column lies. (The clue cells are those with grey outlines orthogonally adjacent to the row/column they rank.) There are no ties in rank. Within the rest of the 15x17 grid: Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of orthogonally connected cells. Regions cannot overlap. Fill each cell with a number that is the size of the region. Regions of the same size cannot share a cell edge.

title: The Dog is Sneaking around in the Fog?
description:
Here's where you can attempt Cookie Crime 1: Hide And Sneak by Sandra & Nala: https://sudokupad.app/sotpbtg8o1 
Placing correct digits might clear some fog. Each row, column, and region contains the digits 1-9 once each. A region is an orthogonally connected collection of cells. The shape and position of the regions have to be determined.
There are 9 blue circles (with thicker outline) in the grid. Each blue circle belongs to a different region. Additionally there are black circles (with thinner outline). These can be in any region and a region can have more than 1 black circle. The digit in a circle counts the number of cells that the circle sees from its own region in the row and column up to the first border including itself. 
A small magenta arrow counts the number of region borders seen in the direction it points. If a cell has more than arrow, they see the same amount of borders in each indicated directions. The outer edges of the grid do not count as borders. On a white dot, digits are consecutive. On a black dot, one digit is double the other.
