title: One Of The Cleverest Sudokus We've EVER Seen: Rat Run 24 (S3: E4)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The new season of Rat Run has been incredible so far but tonight's sudoku, Between You And Me, is simply one of the cleverest puzzles we have ever seen. Marty Sears has outdone himself again - it's close to magic.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/1b3iaeit8s

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths must only converge at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz and Phinx may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but they may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Digits may not repeat within a cage. All cages have the same total, to be deduced. An electricity symbol indicates the cage's shock value. Cages with a shock value of 5 or higher may not be entered. Cages with a shock value lower than 5 are safe to enter. If a red X sits between two digits, they sum to 10. In this experiment, both paths must be a valid 'between line', ie: the highest and lowest digits on a path can be found at its ends (on the rat and the cupcake cell, in some order) and not anywhere else along that path.

description:
Here's where you can try Dutch-pelgänger by ChinStrap: https://sudokupad.app/t4fevoplnv 
Fill each cell of the main 9x9 grid such that every row, column and 3x3 box contains a 0 and eight different digits from 1-9. No two rows, no two columns and no two boxes may be missing the same digit. For each 0 in the grid, the digits missing in its row, column and region must be three different digits. title: You've Never Seen This Sudoku Rule Before!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The extraordinary Kaktuslav is on an absolute roll at the moment and producing masterpiece after masterpiece. Tonight we attempt Sunblock, which features a ruleset we've definitely not seen before! Also do have a go at our brand new competition over on Patreon from the Sudoku Skunkworks, which launched this afternoon.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yeb6vd8pem

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Regions do not overlap. Place the digits 1–9 once each in every row, column, and region. Suns: The digit in a sun counts how many of the up to nine cells in the 3×3 square centered on that sun belong to the same region as the sun (including the sun cell itself). Example: If R4C1 = 3, then exactly three of the cells R3C1, R3C2, R4C1, R4C2, R5C1, and R5C2 belong to the same region as R4C1.

description:

Wow, we were not expecting that. Quadcopter by arctan bears a lot of similarities in its set-up with other sudokus we've seen before (including Aad van de Wetering's 10 Million Views puzzle from a few days ago). title: Are You Good At Mazes? Solve This NEW Rat Run! (S3:E3)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In Simon's opinion, this is one of the MOST extraordinary puzzles from the most extraordinary sudoku series: Rat Run! It's called Notable Differences and Marty Sears has created a test constraint in this one that almost defies belief.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/3pev731294

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths may not share cells except where they meet at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz and Phinx may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant then one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a redcurrant then one is even and the other is odd. If two digits are joined by a grape then they have a difference of at least 5. In this experiment, Finkz and Phinx both visit the same number of cells. Before reaching the cupcake, the Nth digit visited by Finkz and the Nth digit visited by Phinx always have the same difference (to be deduced.) This difference equals the digit on the cupcake cell. Eg: if the 3rd digit visited by Finkz is 5 and the 3rd digit visited by Phinx is 9, the cupcake cell would contain a 4.

title: Colouring Your Sudoku Has Never Been So Fun!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A fabulous idea and execution tonight from James Sinclair in the form of his new puzzle Stickiest Notes. A really original ruleset with some fantastic logic to boot - just a great way to spend some sudoku time :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/stickiest-notes?setting-nogrid=1

A colour-blind friendly version is available here:
https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/stickiest-notes-with-labels?setting-nogrid=1

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally-connected cells. Regions cannot overlap. Place the digits 1-9 once in each row, column, and region. Each region has a corresponding colour. A note outside the grid indicates that the region of that colour contains a run of one or more orthogonally-connected cells (bounded on either side by a region border or the edge of the grid) in that row or column, and the number in the note (if given) is the sum of the digits in these cells. If a region contains multiple sets of orthogonally-connected cells in the same row or column, a note only applies to one of them. When two notes overlap, the note above has a lower sum than the note below (this applies even if a sum is hidden or not given).

Today's introduction is from The Roving by Bonny Light Horseman. There's a great version of the song here:

title: Method to the Madness
description:
Here's where you can attempt Method to the Madness by Merdock: https://sudokupad.app/753umuwjuz 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing correct digits may clear some fog. Digits separated by an X sum to 10, digits separated by a V sum to 5. 
Purple (Howling Mad) lines indicate a sequence of digits where no other specified line type could go:
Renban: Consecutive non-repeating digits;
Nabner: Non-consecutive non-repeating digits;
Parity: Alternating even/odd;
Entropy: Every 3 digits has a [1,2,3], [4,5,6], and [7,8,9] digit;
Modular: Every 3 digits has a [1,4,7], [2,5,8], and [3,6,9] digit;
Dutch Whisper: Adjacent digits differ by at least 4;
Region Sum: Box borders divide lines into segments with the same sum.
Howling Mad lines are always three cells long and are always either strictly vertical or strictly horizontal. Lines cannot overlap each other. No set of digits appears on more than one line. For example, if one line contains 1, 2, and 4, no other line can contain all three of those digits. Given those rules, no further lines are possible.

title: A Sudoku Expert Spills All His Secrets!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In a week of stellar sudoku, it's great to bring you the latest from zetamath (and his friends)! It's called Mosaic and it's actually extremely wonderful. There are several beautiful pieces of logic in this one and Simon has to spill almost all his secrets :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/h2sdbmic8x

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a GW (“German Whisper”) line must differ by at least five. Any set of three adjacent cells along an Ent (Entropy) line must contain a low digit (123), a middle digit (456), and a high digit (789). If two digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. Not all black dots are necessarily given. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.  Not all white dots are necessarily given. Digits along grey lines (“Ten Lines”) must be broken into one or more contiguous groups of cells that sum to ten. Such groups cannot overlap. Digits may repeat within such sums if allowed by other rules. Eg 513173 is a valid fill for a length 6 line, because it can be broken into 5131 and 73, each of which sum to 10. Adjacent digits along a DW (“Dutch Whisper”) line must differ by at least four. Digits along a PR line alternate odd/even. No two digits along a Nab (“Nabner”) line can be consecutive, regardless of their position on the line.

title: Copyrat: Get The Rats Through This Crazy Sudoku! (S3:E2)
description:
[Please do "Like" the video (if you do!) tonight. Because it uploaded late, the algorithm will punish it unless it feels viewers particularly enjoy it.]

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears' Rat Run series reached its second puzzle of the third season and a puzzle called Copyrat. What have Finkz and Phinx been up to and how are you going to get them both to a cupcake? It's not quite as straightforward to figure this one out but every step along the way will leave you with a smile on your face!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/m9qm0m5qj0

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz and Phinx may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Find nine copycat cells in the maze; one in each row, column and 3x3 box, and each containing a different digit. The value of a copycat cell equals the digit in the cell that is 180° rotationally opposite it in the grid. Eg: if r1c3 is a 6 and r9c7 is a copycat cell, then r9c7 will have a value of 6, regardless of what digit it contains. If two cells are joined by a blackcurrant then the value of one is double the value of the other. If two cells are joined by a redcurrant then one has an even value and the other has an odd value. If two cells are joined by a grape then their values have a difference of at least 5. In this experiment, in any 3x3 box, the total value of the cells visited by Finkz is the same as the total value of the cells visited by Phinx. (This total must be determined for each box.)

title: Astronomical Sudoku Alert!
description:
Here's where you can have a go at Doppler Astronomy by Blobz: https://sudokupad.app/blobz/doppler-astronomy 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into galaxies: orthogonally connected groups of cells that have 180 degree rotational symmetry about their centers (marked with a small dot). All cells must be part of a galaxy; no galaxies overlap.
Galaxies are either red-shifted (moving away from the observer), or blue-shifted (moving towards the observer). The measured value of each galaxy is shown; it is the sum of the digits in that galaxy PLUS (blue-shifted) or MINUS (red-shifted) the number of cells in the galaxy.
Dots with a solid black outline indicate "Renban" galaxies, whose digits form an unbroken consecutive sequence in any order. Conversely, dots without a solid black outline indicate galaxies whose digits do NOT form such a sequence. Digits may not repeat within a galaxy.
Five single-cell galaxies — "Dark Stars" — are NOT marked: their locations must be deduced by the solver. All cells (max 8) around a Dark Star belong to regular galaxies. No 3x3 box contains more than one Dark Star. Digits do not repeat amongst the Dark Stars.

title: Fog Sudoku: You've Never Seen This Before!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel today for Wiggel and a puzzle called Purple Lines. It's fog sudoku and this is one of the most original we've seen in a while... definitely give it a try, you WON'T regret it!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/56e3pocc01

Rules:
Purple Lines
by Wiggel
Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1 to 9 once each, in every row, column and box.
The grid is covered in fog, placing correct digits clears the fog somewhere in the grid. 
No guessing is required, of course.
Blue lines are “Modular Lines”, ie every connected run of 3 cells along them must contain one of the digits [147], one of the digits [258] and one of the digits [369].
Red lines are Parity Lines, when going along them, digits alternate between odd and even.
Purple lines, ... - What? The title mentions purple lines? 
What were they again? Maybe they were Renbans?
The digits on a Renban form a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order.
No, that was wrong! No purple line could ever be a valid Renban.
Ah, now I remember! They just combine the rules of the other two lines.
So a purple line is always a valid blue line and a valid red line.
At the same time! Good thing I remembered that.
Now that I'm done explaining the rules, I have to get going.
I really hope the rules will help you with solving the puzzle.

title: Racing all around the Grid  ... wow!
description:
Here's where you can try Grid Racer by Jonesy: https://sudokupad.app/lhid2td2zu 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single closed loop representing the car’s path, viewed from above. The car drives clockwise around the grid through cell centers and moves strictly orthogonally. The path may touch itself orthogonally but must not cross or branch. Cages are obstacles which the car can never enter. The loop must visit each region at least once.
The digit in any cell the loop passes through determines the car’s movement: Odd digits (1,3,5,7,9): go straight. Even digits (2,4,6,8): turn, using absolute numpad directions: 
2 → Up  4 → Left
6 → Right 8 → Down
In each 3×3 box, the sum of the odd digits on the loop equals the sum of the digits inside the cage(s) in that box (multiple visits of the loop contribute to the same total). A region without a cage indicates the sum of odd digits for that region is zero.

title: The Perfect Puzzle for Today
description:
Here's where you can try Nala's Toy Battle by Panthera: https://sudokupad.app/9ecadg11io 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog will clear as correct digits are placed. There is a red cage from r3-r9 and c3-c9 in which Japanese sums colorings will take place, with clues given in c1-2 and r1-2. Clues are colored pink, and if there is a cage there, the sum of the run of pink cells is known to be the small digit in the corner * 10 + the value in the cage. So if a cage had a little 1 and a 4 was placed in it, the JSS clue would be 14. If there is no cage, you know there's a run of coloring, but not what it sums to. 
The clues inside the grid (r1-2 and c1-2) indicate the sums of the contiguous runs found in that row or column that must be shaded. There must be an unshaded cell between runs of the same color. If a row or column is unclued (no pink cells at all), there is no shading in that row or column. Cells joined with a V sum to 5. 4 colored dots in the grid, Green, Red, Blue and Yellow are ratio dots and may represent any ratio from 1:2, 1:3, 1:4, 1:5, 1:6, 1:7, 1:8, or 1:9. It's up to the solver to determine which dot is which type. A pink line is either Renban (consecutive sequence of digits in any order) OR German Whisper (neighbouring digits differ by at least 5. Each line must be determined individually. A circle is odd.

title: Rat Run Season 3!! We've Waited A Year For This Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What a day! It's been a year since Rat Run Episode 20 concluded Season 2 of the world's most popular sudoku series. Today we're delighted to have a go at the puzzle from Episode 1 of season 3, Friendly in which Finkz has been joined by a second rat, Phinx! Marty Sears has done it once again... incredible.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/bbcodg1b5w

Rules:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths may not share cells except for where they meet at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz and Phinx may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant, one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a grape, they have a difference of at least 5. If two digits are joined by a red X, they sum to 10. Finkz and Phinx may not pass directly through a red X. In this experiment, a cell may only be visited by Finkz or Phinx if its digit matches its row number, column number or box number. (Boxes are numbered 1-9 in normal reading order from top left to bottom right.)

We had a new puzzle from Jay Dyer yesterday which was fantastic and now Myxo returns with what must surely be a candidate for puzzle of the year and we're only in January. It's called Entropic Detour, it's had very few solves so far... and when you see it, you might understand why!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/cbbvbid2vt

Rules:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a small white dot must be consecutive. Draw a closed loop into the grid that travels orthogonally between cells and doesn't visit the same cell more than once. The loop must not visit any big circles. The loop acts as an entropic line, i.e. three adjacent digits along the loop must contain one digit from {1,2,3}, one digit from {4,5,6} and one digit from {7,8,9}. The number of loop turns is different in each 3x3 box. A digit in a big circle indicates the number of times the loop turns in that box.

title: The Sudoku Variants just keep on Coming!
description:
Here's where you can attempt SVS #454 - Little Thermometers by Richard Stolk: https://sudokupad.app/2ofk8u9afe 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid indicates the presence of a thermometer that is fully placed in the direction of the arrow where all the digits on the thermometer add to the number of the clue and the bulb is always the closest to the clue. Digits on a thermometer are all different and strictly increasing from the bulb to the tip. Thermometers are mimimally three cells long and they include all possible digits. i.e. the first digit behind the thermometer may not be larger than the last digit on the thermometer, and the last digit before a thermometer may not be smaller than the digit in the bulb. Thermometers may overlap other thermometers.

title: Build Your Own Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We must have missed this sudoku when it originally came out in December. It's called Build Your Own Hitlines and it's by none other than Marty Sears. It's fiendishly clever and the denouement is close to unbelievable - it's like unravelling a Gordian Knot! (Don't forget we're streaming more Blue Prince tonight!)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/u10p16g8n5

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. From each square, draw a valid hitline moving through the centres of cells. Each hitline must occupy at least two cells. Hitlines may travel orthogonally and diagonally between cells, but may not branch, share cells, or cross themselves or each other. Digits may not repeat on a hitline. The small white clue on a square indicates the total sum of all the digits along that hitline that match their position number, with the square itself being position 1. Eg: if a hitline reads 82195 then its square would have a 7 clue, as this is the sum of 2 and 5 which are the only two digits on the line which match their position number (they are in the 2nd position and 5th position.)

title: Will Our Puzzle Expert Make The Same Mistake?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A few weeks ago Simon attempted masetab's first Territories puzzle and almost made a complete mess of it. It took some late fixing to make the solve logical... Now he attempts the second in the series, Non-consecutive Territories and this is every bit as brilliant as the first (and that was very brilliant!)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/h63cv2l7tp

Rules
Fill the grid with digits 1–9, so that each digit appears exactly once in every row and column. All cells except those in cages must be grouped into regions consisting of orthogonally connected cells. Each region contains exactly one circle. The number inside the circle gives the number of cells in its region. No digit may repeat within any cage or any region. In addition, no two digits within the same cage or the same region may be consecutive. Allowed examples: {3,1,5}, {1}, {4,2,9,6}. Two cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits. If two cells are joined by a blue dot, they belong to different regions. Two cells joined by a V contain digits summing to 5. Not all possible dots or symbols are given. The arrow outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.

title: A new Song for the Channel?
description:
Here's where you can try What's the Sequency, Kenneth? (play in chrome) by WEBthe3rd: https://sudokupad.app/7fvnto2d90 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. A correctly placed digit will clear any fog in that cell, and potentially in other cells as well. 
Sequence lines (S) - Thick dark gray lines contain an ordered set of digits with a constant difference between adjacent cells, i.e., 1-2-3, 2-5-8 or 3-3-3, but not 1-3-2.
Palindromes (P) - Light gray lines contain digits that read the same in either direction.
German whispers - Digits separated by a green square must differ by at least 5 from their neighbors on the square.
Parity - Digits separated by a red diamond must differ in parity (even/odd).
Kropki dots - Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive, and not all dots are given.
3-modular lines (3M) - Teal lines contain one each from the sets (147), (258) and (369) for every sequence of three consecutive digits.
Region sum lines (RS) - Blue lines are split by the region boundaries into segments that have the same sum.

title: The IMPOSSIBLE Miracle Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the most amazing miracle sudoku puzzles we've ever seen tonight from Alaric Taqi A. (Crusader175) called Budoka (which we've now understood means "construction" in Polish!) It beggars belief that this can work as a sudoku with no given regions. There's no trickery here; just a short and seemingly underpowered ruleset... and yet!!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/yp4js8z1ck

Rules
Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells, such that every cell is part of exactly one region. Place the digits 1-9 exactly once in each row, column and region. Adjacent digits along a line must either be consecutive and belong to a different region or have a 1:2 ratio and belong to the same region. (A 1:2 ratio means one digit will be double the other.) If 1 and 2 are adjacent along a line, they can satisfy either condition.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An unusual and clever sudoku tonight from damo_89 that one good judge (Erin) says is her favourite puzzle of the year (we're not sure whether she meant 2025 or 2026!). This one involves coordinate arrows but with a doubler twist. Magnificent!

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/by6i2h7toi

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. 9 cells in the grid are “doublers”, one in every row, column, and 3x3 box, each containing a different digit. The value of a doubler cell is double the digit in that cell. Values on an arrow spell the coordinates for the value that is their sum. The row value is on the start of the arrow and the column value on the tip. Eg if an arrow contained the values 15, then a 6 (or a doubled 3) is placed in R1C5. Each arrow indicates a different cell.

title: Space Invaders: The Sudoku!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A week or so ago we were astonished by a sudoku themed on Minesweeper by Michael Lefkowitz and TalkingFredish. Michael returns tonight with another of these impossible-sounding mash-ups in the form of Space Invaders!!  Not only is this wildly imaginative, it's also a brilliant puzzle... Absolute genius.

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/uojuxaw1qw?setting-nogrid=1

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each Invader sums to 10 with a digit in some orthogonally adjacent cell. Digits connected by a 𐌔 always have the same difference. Strategically place 3 turrets into cells in the bottom row. Each turret has as many missiles as the digit in its cell, and can pivot to fire them upwards or diagonally. A turret can destroy an Invader on a digit N by shooting it N times. Each Invader is only shot by one of the turrets. All Invaders must be destroyed!

title: The Sudoku Fog Needs Erasing!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's been a while since we tackled a fog-of-war sudoku puzzle on the channel but we've got a great one tonight in the form of Fog Erasure by R.Mullinix! This is a really clever example actually and you may find yourself having to pause and think a couple of times :)

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/c8shq67xrf

Rules
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog.  Entering correct digits may clear fog. No guessing is required. There is one Eraser Cell in every row, column, and 3x3 box. The nine eraser cells all contain different digits.  The value of an eraser cell is always 0.  The value of non-eraser cells is the digit in the cell. Values along a thermometer increase from bulb to tip. Values in cells joined by a V sum to 5. Values in a cage may not repeat and sum to the total given in the cage’s top left cell.  Digits MAY repeat in a cage. If two cells are joined by a green line the values in those cells must have a difference of at least 5.

title: Solving This Sudoku Is Going On The Top Of My RÉSUMÉ
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight's sudoku elicited perhaps the greatest comment on any puzzle on Logic Masters. The puzzle is called Ten Ring Circus, it's by Jeff Wajes... and the comment was as follows:

"I am going to print out a certificate congratulating myself on completing this puzzle, and I'm going to hang it on my wall, and make sure every guest notices it as they walk in. It'll be the first thing listed on my resume, with the heading "Greatest Accomplishments", when I apply for jobs. When I'm on a date, I'll subtly mention that I solved this Sudoku, so they can see that I can commit to a long-term relationship from the many hours it took to solve. By far the best Sudoku experience I've ever had."

Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/ah1c5p6zcr

Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey line can be divided into segments of contiguous cells, where the digits in each segment sum to 10. These segments cannot overlap and every cell is part of exactly one segment. Place 1-6 in each row, column and 3x2 box. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g., if a purple line contains a 5, then no other purple line in the puzzle may contain a 5:

title: The Sudoku Rat Run Returns!! Happy 2026 :)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What a start to the new year!! Marty Sears delivers a teaser for Rat Run Season 3 in the form of Rat Run: 51 Years Later. This time we have to make the maze :)

As mentioned in yesterday's video, Simon takes a little time at the start of tonight's episode to answer viewer questions. Just skip forward if this isn't interesting to you. And remember that our new Sudoku Hunt launched on Patreon this afternoon AND there was bonus viewer-solve video on the channel this morning!

Tim Paulden's Charity Puzzle hunt, which runs until 18 January, can be found here:
http://www.thexmaspuzzles.com/


Play the puzzle at the links below:

https://sudokupad.app/b7mlk88xmf

Rules
Fill the grid with the digits 0-3 so that each digit appears TWICE in every row, column, and marked 4x2 box. Reconstruct the maze by drawing thick walls along certain cell edges. The wall around the maze perimeter has been drawn already. The digit in a circle indicates how many of that cell's 4 edges contain a wall. The finished maze must have a valid route from the red R (rat) to the blue C (cupcake), without passing through any walls or visiting any cell more than once. No diagonal moves are possible in this maze, due to the brown wall spots on the corners of cells. An edge containing a purple arrow does not contain a wall, and sits between two different digits, with the arrow pointing towards the smaller digit. An arrow can only be passed through in the direction it's pointing. Adjacent digits along the path must sum to at least 3.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Last month, Don won our competition and, very kindly, agreed to make a sudoku video with Simon.  Mark selected the puzzle The Only Constant Is Change by Erin Toler.  This is a brilliant choice as Erin actually featured in our third episode in this series earlier in the year. She was smart as whip then and has now started setting so you can imagine how good this is! Don and I also agreed that Anyday by Derek and the Dominoes is one of the greatest songs of all time :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/erin-toler/the-only-constant-is-change

Rules:
"Do the best you can until you know better. Then, when you know better, do better."
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Echo Lines: Indigo lines are filled with a repeating sequence of one or more different digits. The full sequence must appear at least twice along the line and must always repeat in its entirety. Different lines may contain different sequences.
Nabner lines: No two digits on a yellow line may be the same or consecutive.
Killer Cages: Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the given total.
